為什么推薦入住上海迪士尼度假區酒店?
方便刷項目
入住上海迪士尼度假區的酒店都享有三大權益：優先入園(至多提前1小時進入上海迪士尼樂園)、免費酒店-樂園的往返穿梭巴士/船、免費停車。
優先入園1小時可是黃金時間，你能在這1小時把最熱門的項目都提前刷掉。
買1晚含早的朋友，提前刷完熱門項目後，可以回酒店悠閑享用自助早餐，還有機會見到迪士尼朋友們。
買2晚的朋友，下午也可以回酒店休息一下，充好電後繼續入園看煙花、買買買。
樂園酒店的早餐自助餐廳是盧米亞廚房，以《美女與野獸》為主題。
酒店客人的優先入園入口是在單獨的迪士尼小鎮安檢口，人會少很多，不用和早享卡的遊客們卷。
免費行李寄存
在樂園裏寄存行李大概需要80元，而入住迪士尼酒店退房後可以免費寄存行李。
並且可以選擇送到迪士尼樂園入口的遊客中心，一天玩累了之後可以直接帶著行李箱走，不用再回到酒店去取行李了。
方便買買買
兩家酒店一樓都配有商店，還沒入園就可以開始買買買了。另外還可以買到特選商品，特選商品在樂園裏可是需要抽簽中了才能買的。
如果你在樂園裏買了紀念品，又不想拎著購物袋遊玩，那可以使用商品領取服務(免費)，可以送到樂園大門口或者你入住的酒店商店。
各種娛樂活動
2家酒店都配備了遊泳池、兒童遊樂屋、多家餐廳。酒店每天也會有不同的活動可以探索，大人小孩都能玩個大半天。
辦理入住時，小朋友也可以在大堂看迪士尼動畫，遛娃很省心。
沉浸式迪士尼氛圍
樂園酒店更加夢幻，讓你踏進酒店那刻就變身王子公主，改為沉浸在童話世界。最近還新出了求婚套餐，有需求的可以看看。
在樂園酒店，你能隨機碰見米奇和他的朋友們，房間床頭是會“放煙花”的，大堂有迪士尼音樂現場演奏，公區陽台就能看到樂園煙花。
樂園酒店的早餐自助餐廳是盧米亞廚房，以《美女與野獸》為主題。
用餐時還有迪士尼朋友們來每一桌互動。
玩具總動員酒店一定是玩總IP粉的大愛，滿滿的玩總元素。
花園裏有巨大的胡迪、巴斯光年、三眼仔火箭發射台，在色彩明亮的酒店裏走著走著好像自己也變成了安迪的玩具，進入了玩具的世界。
玩具總動員酒店的早餐自助餐廳是陽光食彙，雖然沒有迪士尼朋友來互動，但是餐品也是各種玩總風格。
所以如果想要更省心、更沉浸玩上迪，建議是可以在迪士尼酒店住個1、2晚的，體驗絕對會升級很多。
2)上海迪士尼1日遊（早享卡提前1小時入園+入園有導遊全程陪同6小時+包含8-10個經典項目+帶看花車巡遊）
門票預定：Trip | Klook
上海迪士尼為什么值得玩?
1)最新迪士尼，科技感十足
上海迪士尼樂園目前是全世界最新的迪士尼樂園。
雖然上周迪士尼剛官宣了第七座迪士尼樂園(阿布紮比)的消息，但是目前我們上迪還是穩穩最新的、科技感十足的樂園。
特別是加勒比海盜和去年剛開幕的瘋狂動物城園區，各種技術都讓人贊歎，咱們後面慢慢介紹。
2)面積大，項目多
上海迪士尼整個度假區的面積僅次於美國奧蘭多迪士尼。
上迪真的很大，8大園區、2大酒店，還有1個配套的迪士尼小鎮。
我每次去上迪，一整天的步數都在2W打底，所以想要玩遍上海迪士尼，建議是選擇玩兩天。
3)達菲家族元素多
現在提到上迪，第一印象肯定就是我們玲娜貝兒。
達菲家族成員大多數是東迪開始衍生的IP，但是它們在上迪存在感一定是最強的。
專門的七寶商店都有好幾家，更別提買不完的上新商品、季節限定表演、每年都不同的服裝...
雖然作為迪士尼老粉，我更喜歡經典IP。但是達菲家族周邊實在是太可愛了，這幾年也是忍不住買了一櫃子...
所以對於喜歡達菲家族的朋友來說，上海迪士尼絕對能滿足你。
4)超多周邊可以買買買
亞洲的三家迪士尼周邊都很值得買，上新速度快，設計也很在線。
上迪的周邊更是融合了中國特色，你能買到小籠包奇奇蒂蒂或者是上海灘米奇米妮。
達菲家族每年還會有中秋、春節系列。前段時間還出了青花瓷系列呢。
我相信很難有能空手離開上迪的遊客吧。
5)季節限定活動多
每年不同時間都會有限定的季節性活動，四季都會有不同的驚喜。
往年季節活動圖，具體以實際活動為准
給大家Po個全年大概的活動時間，照片都是往年拍的，僅供參考。
春天
春日活動，彩色慶典花車巡遊、賞春賞花。
公主月，可以見到稀有公主王子，還有瘋狂動物城主題活動可以打卡
漫威月，可以見到稀有超級英雄。
夏天
皮克斯月，可以見到稀有皮克斯夥伴。
夏日活動，城堡“潑水節”和達菲朋友夏日巡遊。
秋天
達菲月，達菲和好夥伴們會穿上中秋服飾。
萬聖節，有迪士尼反派夜間巡遊，還可以打扮成迪士尼朋友入園。
冬天
冰雪節，冬日巡遊、米奇大街飄雪、聖誕樹點燈。
元旦，跨年大煙花。
春節，搖擺舞、新年限定大煙花。
夏日活動快來了。大概是6月到8月，覆蓋整個暑假。往年夏日活動比較特色的就是夏日狂歡節城堡秀和繽紛夏日巡遊。
溫馨提醒：准備好雨衣，“澡堂式”水花可不是開玩笑的。
迪士尼朋友們也會換上夏日新裝，期待和你見面。
每年活動也會有一些變動和小驚喜。今年會有什么，可以期待一下哦。
上海迪士尼樂園怎么玩更省心?
作為常年遊客量幾萬的“內卷王”，不管是項目還是互動，排隊時間都很長。
想要玩得省心，接下來劃重點。
1)下載上海迪士尼官方APP
APP最主要的當然是查看地圖和排隊時間，方便計劃下一步去遊玩哪個項目。
APP下載網址：https://www.shanghaidisneyresort.com/information/download-shanghai-disney-mobile-app
除此之外，樂園相關信息基本都能在APP上找到。
比如門票綁定、尊享卡購買、特定商品購買資格抽簽、遊樂項目身高要求、活動演出時間、商店、餐廳、服務設施等等...
2)計劃遊玩路線
計劃好遊玩路線就成功了一半，尤其是對於一天內想刷完大多數項目的遊客來說。
親子遊、情侶遊、朋友遊想打卡的項目會有所不同，所以在這裏也只給大家做一個簡單的路線推薦，具體還得再自己DIY一下。
推薦路線：瘋狂動物城(熱力追蹤)-夢幻世界(小矮人過山車)-寶藏灣(加勒比海盜沉落寶藏之戰)-探險島(翱翔·飛越地平線)-明日世界(創極速光輪)-玩具總動員(抱抱龍沖天賽車)-米奇大街(購物/花車/煙花)
3)購買尊享服務
尊享服務有尊享卡和尊享導覽。
尊享卡相當於走單獨的免排隊通道，最簡單粗暴的氪金力量。每個項目都可以單獨購買尊享卡，或者也可以買尊享套餐。
建議購買尊享卡的項目：熱力追蹤、翱翔·飛越地平線、七個小矮人礦山車、極速創光輪、加勒比沉落寶藏之戰、抱抱龍沖天賽車。
尊享導覽更省心但更貴，對於普通遊客來說也不太建議購買了。
4)入住迪士尼酒店
房間預訂
入住玩具總動員酒店和上海迪士尼樂園酒店，可享提前1小時入園。
這1小時可是黃金時間，可以把最熱門的幾個項目先刷掉，立省幾小時。
提前入園通道是單獨在迪士尼小鎮入口，人會比早享卡入口少很多。
另外也有免費接駁班車/船直接到樂園門口，中途玩累了回酒店休息一下也很方便。
5)購買早享卡
如果覺得尊享卡或者迪士尼酒店超預算了，也可以選擇更實惠的早享卡，大概199元左右，高峰日會更貴一些。
早享卡可以提前1小時入園，和入住迪士尼酒店一樣的權益。
不過早享卡是在樂園正門入園，比起入住迪士尼酒店，需要更早一點去安檢口排隊。
早享卡在入園前7天開放購買，可以去小程序買。一般是0點-0點10分放票。
6)善用單人通道
很多熱門項目是有單人通道的，比如小矮人、熱力追蹤、創極速光輪。一般會比正常排隊時間快一倍以上。
單人通道的定義是補位前面的空缺座位，如果不介意和朋友分開坐的話，是可以一起排單人通道隊伍的。
7)善用無包免安檢通道
上迪的安檢隊伍很長，所以如果不帶包(東西拿手上或者揣褲包裏都可以)的話可以走單獨的無包通道，高峰時間段甚至能省下1個小時。
8)錯峰出行
一般來說，周中的幾個工作日客流量會比較小。
可以通過票價和早享卡價格判斷客流量，價格越高客流量越大。
9)交通選擇
自駕：米奇停車場(14元/小時，112元封頂)，到檢票口需要走大天橋。
迪士尼小鎮停車場(30元/小時，240元封頂)，貴但近，入園離園都很方便。
打車：建議打出租車不要打網約車，到迪士尼出租車上下客點(只有出租車可以到，網約車不行)。離檢票口最近，不需要走大天橋。
地鐵：從市區出發可以乘坐11號線到終點站，步行到檢票口;
從虹橋機場/高鐵站出發可以乘坐市域線到上海國際度假區，再坐巴士/打車。
10）周邊住宿推薦
三簡民宿(迪士尼二期店)
這家具有摩洛哥風格的民宿，乍一看像一座異域城堡。整個民宿都很有設計感。
“三簡”目前共有三期，最好看的就是這二期，房間內部裝修十分上檔次，浴室的設計也特別有品位。最關鍵是民宿還提供免費接駁車接送迪士尼的服務。
地址：川沙鎮牌樓村邱家宅23號
價格：612元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海火星島休閑度假民宿
這是全網被贊爆了的一家民宿，暮色下純白建築仿佛置身於聖托裏尼。民宿從內到外都是純白設計，融合了外星球的元素，特色的樹屋、菠蘿屋，像極了海綿寶寶的家。
公共區域有很多打卡點，天空之境、天梯、無邊泳池和洞穴，非常出片。更重要的是，在民宿露台上就可以看到迪士尼的煙花。
地址：川沙新鎮嶺七路10號
價格：470元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海左汐度假別墅
這家民宿有著童話般的環境，香樟大樹、竹林、草坪，甚至還有一條河作為背景。
室外還有樹屋棧道、拍照水池、透明滑梯、鳥窩、秋千等超多攝影空間，給人一種在置身歐洲度假的感覺。
地址：川沙新鎮果園村434號
價格：632元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海迪士尼樂園哪些項目值得玩?
上海迪士尼樂園有8大園區：米奇大街、奇想花園、夢幻世界、明日世界、迪士尼·皮克斯玩具總動員、瘋狂動物城、寶藏灣、探險島。
想要一次玩遍所有項目、看完各種演出...是不太可能的，所以給大家推薦一下比較值得玩的項目。直接沖不會錯。
米奇大街
推薦：迪士尼朋友互動、花車巡遊
在米奇大街，最特色的就是你能見到超多迪士尼朋友。喜歡互動的朋友能在這蹲一天。
這裏有各種紀念品商店，在甜心糖果可以買到達菲家族商品。在M大街購物廊能買到經典迪士尼角色商品。
餐飲：米奇好夥伴集市提供麻辣燙、牛排炒面等;琦妙美味屋提供可麗餅、蛋糕等
迪士尼朋友互動：米奇米妮、唐老鴨黛絲、奇奇蒂蒂、高飛布魯托、達菲雪莉玫、星黛露可琦安、傑拉多尼奧樂米拉
奇想花園
推薦：奇夢之光幻影秀
上海迪士尼的煙花秀很震撼大氣，特別是複仇者聯盟那段特別燃。玩上迪一定要看完煙花秀才是最值的。
奇想花園其他的玩樂比較適合小朋友玩，在這也能找到不錯的花車觀賞位置。
其他玩樂項目：小飛象、幻想曲旋轉木馬、米奇俱樂部、漫威英雄總部
餐飲：花間美味、提摩太小吃等小吃
迪士尼朋友互動：米奇、複仇者聯盟英雄
夢幻世界
推薦：七個小矮人礦山車、小飛俠天空奇遇
小矮人過山車建議入園盡早沖，下午排隊時間都會很長。
身高97cm以上的小朋友就可以玩的過山車，基本沒有失重感。途中還能看到小矮人們挖礦工作，小礦車仿佛帶著你穿越進了《白雪公主》的故事。
小飛俠天空奇遇也是很夢幻的寶藏項目，跟著彼得潘一起探險，仙塵灑出來的時候還是很感動的。
旋轉瘋蜜罐現在已經成為“男朋友挨罵打卡點”，來這裏必須要出片!
其他玩樂項目：小熊維尼曆險記、漫遊童話時光、晶彩奇航、愛麗絲夢遊仙境迷宮
餐飲：皮諾丘鄉村廚房提供披薩、豬腳飯等;老藤樹食棧提供烤牛肉、烤雞等
迪士尼朋友互動：迪士尼公主、小熊維尼和他的朋友們
明日世界
推薦：創極速光輪
上海迪士尼樂園可是第一座有創極速光輪的樂園。進入“創”的電子網絡世界，黑暗轉向、室外極速，算是上海迪士尼樂園第二刺激的項目了。如果你看過《創戰紀》電影，會更有代入感。
明日世界主打現代科幻感，在這裏能遇到各位複仇者聯盟英雄們，晚上在E空間俱樂部還有DJ帶你“蹦迪”。
其他玩樂項目：巴斯光年星際營救、太空幸會史迪奇、噴氣背包飛行器
餐飲：星露台餐廳提供漢堡、炸雞等
迪士尼朋友互動：複仇者聯盟英雄
迪士尼·皮克斯玩具總動員
推薦：抱抱龍沖天賽車、胡迪牛仔嘉年華
抱抱龍沖天賽車我願稱為上海迪士尼樂園最刺激項目，因為失重感很強，特別是第一排和最後一排。喜歡體驗失重感的朋友們一定不要放過這個抱抱龍。
胡迪牛仔嘉年華是最近發現的寶藏項目，以前以為只適合小朋友玩，沒想到“甩驢”竟然這么有意思，配上音樂更歡樂。
“變成玩具”進入玩具們的世界，可以見到最喜歡的玩具總動員朋友們。這裏的色彩飽和度很高，不管是白天、夜晚都很適合拍照。
迪士尼在這裏有自己的“賭場”，比如釣火腿豬、三眼仔打槍、賭抱抱龍。我玩過好多次了，至今沒有中過，有中過的朋友可以分享一下經驗...
其他玩樂項目：彈簧狗團團轉
餐飲：草莓熊餐盒提供披薩、炸雞
迪士尼朋友互動：《玩具總動員》胡迪、巴斯光年、抱抱龍
瘋狂動物城
推薦：熱力追蹤
全球第一個熱力追蹤，一定要玩。加入動物城警察局，跟著朱迪尼克抓捕壞綿羊。
排隊區很精彩，運用了最新技術的豹警官和牛局長非常逼真。
有時候進入瘋狂動物城園區是需要額外排隊的，如果購買了尊享卡是可以免園區入口排隊 + 免熱力追蹤排隊，所以在客流量大的日子，買熱力追蹤的尊享卡是最值的。
瘋狂動物城是去年新開的園區，各種1:1複刻電影場景，動物城粉狂喜。
還有好多有趣的彩蛋，比如售賣的飲料是百事可鹿、咩年達、7犀，紅綠燈上顯示的不是小人是大象，就連停車位、健身房都設計成大中小來給不同體型的動物用。
雖然這個園區只有一個玩樂項目，但是主題區的有趣程度絕對能硬控你一小時。還有白天限定的動物城生活秀，可以來看看動物們的家長裏短。
餐飲：大象甜品店提供各式甜品;動物城食集可以買到電影裏的爪爪棒冰
迪士尼朋友互動：《瘋狂動物城》朱迪尼克
寶藏灣
推薦：加勒比海盜沉落寶藏之戰
這是我個人認為上海迪士尼最出彩的項目。投影技術+巨幅屏幕，玩的時候真的會不禁發出“wow”。
大船的機制讓這個項目排隊效率很高，基本都在30分鍾以內。結尾還會有2種不同的大結局隨機出現，很有意思。
整個寶藏灣充滿海盜元素，萬聖節期間還有海盜出沒“打劫”，還可以帶上你的迪士尼朋友玩偶一起“蹦迪”。
其他玩樂項目：船奇戲水灘、探秘海妖複仇號、探險家獨木舟
餐飲：巴波薩燒烤提供豬肋排飯、牛排炒面等;土圖嘉風味提供火雞腿
迪士尼朋友互動：《加勒比海盜》傑克船長
探險島
推薦：翱翔·飛越地平線
這是上海迪士尼的老熱門項目了，在熱力追蹤開幕之前，一直是大家早起入園首沖的項目。
跟著雷鳥婆婆進行一場環球之旅，我對非洲大草原的青草味印象特別深刻。
探險島還有一個整個園區排隊時間最長的項目，常年300分鍾起，那就是和玲娜貝兒見面。很多喜歡互動的朋友也會購買早享卡就為了沖玲娜貝兒互動，不過她真的能給你很足的情緒價值，不愧是銷冠。
其他玩樂項目：古跡探索營、雷鳴山漂流
餐飲：達菲好友歡慶堂提供雞腿飯、烤魚等
迪士尼朋友互動：玲娜貝兒、奇奇蒂蒂、《飛屋環遊記》凱文、逗逗、小羅
上海迪士尼樂園哪些演出值得看?
除了必看的煙花秀和各種季節限定演出以外，上海迪士尼還有幾個特別精彩的演出。迪士尼出品，不容錯過。
米奇妙遊童話書
在香港迪士尼樂園我就特別喜歡這個演出，不過香港迪士尼演出對白是粵語，所以上海迪士尼的體驗會更沉浸。近距離欣賞耳熟能詳的迪士尼歌曲，與23位摯愛的迪士尼朋友們一起歡唱。
表演位於米奇大街，需要注意的是只有在APP完成預約才能入場。提前排隊能有更好的位置，當然也可以選擇購買尊享卡提前入場選最佳觀賞位置。
風暴來臨：傑克船長之驚天特技大冒險
加勒比海盜影迷必看，非常入戲的演繹，配上雜技以及場景變動。夏天來這吹吹空調也是很舒服的。
其他演出
冰雪奇緣：歡唱盛會比較適合小朋友，畢竟艾莎女王是小朋友們的最愛。
太空幸會史迪奇也適合小朋友，史迪仔會和你實時互動。
去年夏季限定的節奏探險之旅也很推薦，許願今年會返場吧。
2026上海迪士尼度假區十周年慶典系列活動
達菲月
在上海迪士尼度假區的10歲生日慶典之際，今年九月的達菲月以達菲和朋友們的溫暖友誼為靈感，邀請遊客加入他們，共赴為期一整個月的全新冒險。
今年達菲月迎來重磅驚喜，上海迪士尼度假區首次攜手享譽業界的上海美術電影制片廠，聯合推出達菲和朋友們的首部動畫微電影。作品將經典國產動畫美學元素與達菲和朋友們的暖心故事巧妙融合，為萌趣夥伴們打造了一段奇妙旅程。此次跨界合作的創意靈感也將全方位落地度假區，融入園區主題裝飾、達菲和朋友們的全新限定造型、獨家商品及特色餐飲體驗中，遊客將處處偶遇驚喜，收獲沉浸式遊玩新體驗。
達菲月期間，度假區將以萌趣滿滿的裝飾迎接遊客。園區內精心打造了多處主題打卡點與拍照牆，融入仙桃、葫蘆、金魚等極具寓意的經典元素，搭配以達菲和朋友們專屬柔和色調精心設計的條幅與絲帶裝飾，氛圍感十足。遊客可置身濃濃秋日氛圍中，邂逅達菲和朋友們，定格溫馨美好瞬間。

title: 上海豫园攻略 2026：门票、开放时间、旺季与路线
text:
最后核实：2026-08-08官方网站↗
1核心亮点
豫园是一座以层层借景取胜的古典园林：墙洞显露假山，亭廊框住池水，短短几步就改变空间尺度。不要把收费的历史园林与外围商业街区混为一谈。九曲桥、中心水面周边和豫园商城公共通行区域通常免费，但临时管控或收费活动可能改变进入方式。
常见开放09:00–16:30
停止入园16:00
闭园⚠️ 周一，法定节假日除外
建议时长1–2小时
2门票与预约
历史园林收费，外围商城和九曲桥公共区域通常免费。旺季为4月1日–6月30日、9月1日–11月30日。园林常见开放时间为09:00–16:30，16:00停止入园，通常周一闭园（法定节假日除外）。票价、时间和活动管控可能变化，请按参观日期核对官方公告。
📌 历史园林—旺季以当期官方票价为准旺季：4月1日–6月30日、9月1日–11月30日。历史园林—淡季以当期官方票价为准优惠资格和证件规则需按当期规定核对。九曲桥与商城公共区通常免费特殊活动与客流管控期间可能另有安排。
⚠️周一闭园：园林通常周一闭园，法定节假日除外。外围商业区可能照常营业，因此从外观看似仍然开放。
💡当天核对：09:00–16:30、16:00停止入园是常见安排，并非永久保证；维修或节庆期间请查官方通知。
⭐我们的首选推荐含推广链接
Klook
查询豫园园林门票与上海导览
仅选择说明清楚的豫园园林门票或导览产品。确认产品覆盖的是收费历史园林，而非仅指免费商城公共区，并核对日期、证件、核销、语言与退改条件。
✓区分收费园林入园与免费商城公共区
✓核对参观日期、闭园通知与核销步骤
✓确认导览语言与具体包含项目
✓预订前阅读退改条款查看豫园与上海导览产品→
披露：这是推广链接。通过它购买我们可能获得少量佣金，你支付的价格不会因此增加。我们只推荐自己会用的产品。
3交通与到达
地铁豫园站最方便。周边老城厢适合步行，但节庆期间客流很大。
🚇豫园站地铁票价
地铁10、14号线，按豫园与商城指示步行，注意区分园林售票入口和商业街。
🚶从外滩步行免费
可从外滩经老城厢步行串联，巷道密集需多留导航时间。
⚠️节庆客流：灯会等节庆期间，外围公共区域可能实施单向通行、预约或限流，请按当期通知。
4路线与拍照
先在体力和光线较好时进入收费园林，再游览通常免费的商城公共区域，避免混淆两者。
🗺️推荐路线
1
收费园林入口
确认开放与票务条件，在停止入园时间前进入。
2
假山、厅堂与池水
沿框景和漏窗慢行，不要只直奔最大的厅堂。
3
九曲桥
出园后前往公共水面区域，拥挤时顺人流通行。
4
商城街巷
最后逛商业街与小吃，点单前先看菜单和价格。
📸最佳拍照位
园林长廊
用门洞和花窗框住假山与亭台。
九曲桥水面
早晨倒影更清晰，团队客也通常少于中午。
传统屋脊
长焦可从现代招牌和人群中提取层叠屋檐。
5餐饮与住宿
南翔小笼小笼包按店铺浮动外卖窗口与堂食楼层排队、价格可能不同，先看菜单。老城厢小吃甜咸点心¥10–60+最拥挤的店不一定最好，可比较周边选择。
6贴士与避坑
✓接近开园时进入园林更安静，商城通常越晚越拥挤。
✓如果只看九曲桥和商城公共区，不要误买所谓“豫园套票”。
✓跨城前往前先核对周一与法定节假日安排。
✓狭窄廊道尽量用小包，商城拥挤时看好随身物品。
7常见问题
上海豫园免费吗？+
历史园林通常收费；九曲桥和豫园商城公共区域通常免费，但特殊活动和客流管控期间可能另有安排。豫园旺季是什么时候？+
旺季为4月1日–6月30日和9月1日–11月30日。参观前请在官方公告中核对当期票价。豫园周一闭园吗？+
园林通常周一闭园，法定节假日除外。外围商铺可能营业，应查看园林自身公告而非商城时间。豫园开放时间是几点？+
常见开放时间为09:00–16:30，16:00停止入园。维修、节假日和活动可能调整，需按日期核对。豫园需要逛多久？+
收费园林建议1–2小时，九曲桥、商城和用餐另加时间；节庆限流期间需预留更多时间。
顺路一起去
上海的其他景点，按真实行程搭配推荐
外滩·南京路
从古典园林围墙走到开阔滨江，是紧凑的市中心同日路线。
上海法租界漫步
对照上海两层历史：老城厢园林技艺与20世纪住宅街区。
出行前必读
这个景点会用到的实用指南

title: The Former French Concession, Shanghai: Is It Worth Visiting
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
The Former French Concession, Shanghai: Is It Worth Visiting？
We will say yes, if you want to experience Shanghai beyond the postcard skyline. And, no, if you only want famous landmarks.
The Former French Concession is a large historic area, worth about 1–2 hours on a first trip, especially if you enjoy walking around slowly for architecture, cafés, and seeing how old Shanghai still fits into everyday city life.
To see the Former French Concession, pick one compact neighborhood, take your time strolling around, and stop when the experience feels complete.
For most first-time visitors, the best choice is Wukang Road → Anfu Road.
What's Actually Worth Your Time?
Choose Your FFC Route That Suits Your Time
When Is the Best Time to Visit
FAQs
What Is Actually Worth Seeing in the Former French Concession?
For a 1–2 hour walk, choose one or two roads and a commercial area for a complete atmospheric experience.
Wukang Road: A Must for First-timers
Wukang Road
This is where you should come for the classic Former French Concession look.
Walk slowly, and look up from time to time. The best part is the sequence of plane trees, villas, apartment buildings, balconies, and quiet residential lanes.
Wukang Mansion is the visual landmark, but the surrounding streets are what make the area worth walking.
Anfu Road: Best for Cafés and Modern Shanghai
Anfu Road direction sign board
Anfu Road gives you the other half of the experience.
Come here when you want to stop for coffee, browse small shops, or watch the street become busier around lunchtime.
This is where the Former French Concession feels most like a living neighborhood rather than an architectural open-air museum.
Fuxing Road: Best for a Quieter Walk
Fuxing Park at Fuxing Road
Turn toward Fuxing Road for less touristy stops.
You will see more residential lanes and fewer commercial storefronts.
This is the side to choose when your idea of sightseeing is simply walking, looking around, and slowing down.
Xintiandi: Worth Combining, Not Worth Forcing Into a Short Walk
Lanes of Shanghai Xintiandi
Xintiandi is polished, commercial, and redeveloped. 
It keeps traditional Shikumen architecture, and is useful when you want restaurants, shopping, air-conditioning, or a more comfortable break.
But it should not replace the street-level experience of Wukang Road and Anfu Road.
And do not assume it is next door: Wukang Road and Xintiandi are about 4 km apart.
Tianzifang: A Maze of Lilongs, Skippable if You Are Short on Time
Shanghai Tianzifang
Tianzifang still preserves the authentic lilong life, and walking into it, a maze of narrow alleyways packed with small shops, still gives you the feeling of stepping back into the 20th century.
Although it has declined somewhat, it is still very lively on holidays and weekends.
Worth a look if you enjoy quirky shopping and don't mind the bustle; skip if you want space, quiet, or are on a tight schedule.
6-Day Beijing and Shanghai Tour A Tale of Two Cities 
Choose Your FFC Route That Suits Your Time
The Former French Concession Map
1–2 Hours: Wukang Road → Anfu Road
This is our recommended first-time route. It gives you enough time to appreciate the architecture without turning the visit into a checklist.
Start around Wukang Road. You will walk through the historic residential streets, pause for photos, and continue north toward Anfu Road.
Allow 20–30 minutes for a coffee or bakery stop rather than trying to squeeze in another major attraction.
You will finish with the part of the district that feels most alive: shops opening, people meeting friends, and cafés spilling onto the street.
If you have more time to explore, you can take a taxi to Xintiandi or Tianzifang to see the clever integration of historical buildings and modern commercial spaces.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
3 Hours or More: Consider a Historic Themed Route for a Deeper Dive
If you're looking for more than a pleasant walk, this route introduces you to the district's hidden history.
Your walk will be guided from Fuxing Park and Sinan Mansions to Donghu Hotel, and end at the Wukang Mansion, following the life of Du Yuesheng, Shanghai's most infamous gangster-turned-power-broker, to show you a different side of the district.
Passing by today's peaceful architecture, it is hard to imagine that behind it lie bloody suppression, armed clashes, and layers of power, ambition, and memory.
Less Than 1 Hour: Wukang Road + Xintiandi
It is a taste of the Former French Concession, not a full visit.
With less than 1 hour, just tick off Wukang Mansion, look at the villas and plane trees, take your photos, and leave. Then you can take a taxi straight to Xintiandi for a short stroll, or simply end here.
Do not try to walk to Xintiandi from Wukang Road.
Wukang Road to Xintiandi is about 4.2 km on foot, so walking between the two takes roughly 50 minutes.
When Is the Best Time to Visit FFC?
8:30–10:00 AM: Best for Local Life and Quiet Streets
Morning on Wukang Road, Shanghai
This is our top choice for a first visit.
Start around 8:30 or 9:00 AM if you want quieter streets and a stronger sense of the neighborhood before the sightseeing crowds build.
You may see residents walking dogs, people picking up breakfast, and office workers moving through the streets.
You also get the advantage of cooler temperatures, which matters on hot Shanghai days.
2:00–4:30 PM: Best for Cafés and a Slow Afternoon
Find a café for a rest on Anfu Road
Choose the afternoon when you care more about cafés, shops, and a relaxed pace.
Take a walk for about an hour. Stop for coffee. Then continue exploring the streets.
This works particularly well when you target the Former French Concession as your slower afternoon experience, rather than the first attraction of the day.
After Sunset: Skip It for Architecture
Night view of Wukang Road, Shanghai
Do not come here at night specifically to "see the Former French Concession."
Once it gets dark, you lose much of what makes the area special: the building designs, balconies, plane-tree canopy, and residential streetscape.
Come in the evening only when you have a specific restaurant, bar, or dinner reservation in mind.
9-Day Beijing ,Xian and Shanghai Tour China Family Classic Tour 
FAQs About the Former French Concession
Can You Go Inside the Old Houses?
Former Residence of Zhou Enlai (Shanghai)
Usually, no. Most historic residences are still private homes, offices, or other working buildings.
You can walk along the streets, photograph exteriors, and look into public lane entrances, but you should not treat historic residences as open museums.
For an interior experience, we will choose several buildings that officially admit visitors, such as the Soong Ching-ling Memorial Residence and Xuhui Old Houses Art Center.
Instead of repeatedly wondering which buildings you can enter, you can focus on the streets and let the guide do the reservations and explain what you are seeing.
Is It Worth Visiting With Kids or Senior Travelers?
Yes, but do not turn it into a long-distance walking tour.
For families, the 1–2-hour Wukang Road → Anfu Road route is the better choice.
You can stop for drinks, coffee, food, or a break whenever needed.
The experience also works well for teenagers because it combines architecture with cafés, shops, photography, and ordinary Shanghai street life rather than requiring them to spend hours inside museums.

title: Zhujiajiao Water Town: How to See Its Less Touristy Side
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Zhujiajiao Water Town: How to See Its Less Touristy Side
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Sep. 10, 2026 
If you have only 1–2 days in Shanghai, skip Zhujiajiao and focus on the Bund, Yu Garden, the Former French Concession, and the city's skyline.
But if you have 3 days or more, Zhujiajiao is worth a half-day, especially if you want a slower contrast to central Shanghai.
The trick is to avoid spending your whole visit on the main canal streets. Give yourself 3–4 hours to mix residential lanes, old gardens, stone bridges, and quiet canal views.
Is Zhujiajiao Worth Half a Day?
Zhujiajiao Less-touristy Route
Should You Take a Boat in Zhujiajiao?
Is Zhujiajiao Suitable for Children and Older Travelers?
When Is the Best Time to Visit Zhujiajiao
How to Get to Zhujiajiao
Is Zhujiajiao Worth Half a Day?
Zhujiajiao Water Town in summer season
Our picks:
1–2 days in Shanghai: Skip Zhujiajiao.
3 days: Optional. Go if you have already covered the main sights and want a slower half-day outside central Shanghai.
4+ days: Recommended. You have enough time to add Zhujiajiao without taking time away from Shanghai's major sights.
Yes, Zhujiajiao is a real historic town. If you want to experience a Jiangnan water town without leaving Shanghai for a full day, this is it.
However, it is not an untouched village. The main streets have souvenir shops, snack stalls, restaurants, boat rides, and plenty of visitors. That means your experience depends heavily on when you arrive and where you walk.
If you arrive on a weekday around 8:30–9:00 AM, you can start with quieter residential lanes before the busiest part of the town fills up.
If you only have one full day in Shanghai, this journey to the western suburbs is not the best use of your time.
Unsure whether Zhujiajiao fits your Shanghai itinerary? We can help you compare it with Suzhou, Hangzhou, or another water town before you give up half a day of your trip.
The Best Zhujiajiao Half-Day Route: See the Town, Not Just the Tourist Street
Route: Visitor Center → West Well Street (西井街) → Kezhi Garden (课植园) & Hexin Garden (和心园) → Fangsheng Bridge (放生桥) → Jiangnan First Tea House (江南第一茶楼) → Tai'an Bridge (泰安桥) → Lang Bridge (廊桥) → City God Temple (城隍庙) → Daqing Post Office (大清邮局)
Distance: Roughly 4–5 km (around 7,000–9,000 steps)
Time needed: About 3–4 hours at a relaxed pace
Don't try to turn it into a checklist. The quieter lanes between the landmarks are part of the experience, rather than being hurried from one crowded photo spot to another.
1. Start at West Well Street, Not Fangsheng Bridge
Alleys of the Zhujiajiao Water Town, Shanghai
When you arrive at the visitor center, don't immediately follow the crowd toward the main canal and Fangsheng Bridge.
Turn into West Well Street (西井街) first.
The atmosphere changes quickly. Instead of souvenir shops and tour groups, you'll see residential lanes, older houses, local shops, and people going about their daily routines.
If you have another 30–45 minutes, continue toward East Well Street (东井街). It is a useful extension when you want more residential scenery rather than another landmark.
2. Don't Skip the Gardens: Both Are Worth Visiting
Kezhi Garde in Zhujiajiao Water Town
The canals and bridges show you the postcard side of the town. Kezhi Garden and Hexin Garden show you how wealthy local families actually lived and how Jiangnan garden design worked. They are also a good way to step away from the busiest commercial streets.
Current prices are:
Kezhi Garden: ¥20
Hexin Garden: ¥30
Shanghai Helong Art Gallery: ¥20
Three-attraction joint ticket: ¥60
Kezhi Garden (课植园) is the larger of the two, with more space to explore and a mix of traditional Jiangnan garden design and Western-style architectural elements.
Hexin Garden (和心园) is smaller but more intimate, with its own gardens, historic buildings, and collections.
We recommend both rather than choosing between them. They are different enough that visiting one does not make the other feel repetitive, and together they give you a much better sense of Zhujiajiao beyond its canals and tourist streets.
The paid attractions are open 8:30 AM–5:00 PM. If you buy the ¥60 joint ticket online, you need to exchange it for a physical ticket by 3:00 PM.
For this route, visit the gardens before Fangsheng Bridge. That way, you see the quieter historic side first and leave the busiest canal area for the classic views later.
3. Walk to Fangsheng Bridge for the Classic Zhujiajiao View
Fangsheng Bridge in Zhujiajiao Water Town
Now head toward Fangsheng Bridge (放生桥).
Built in 1571, it is one of Zhujiajiao's defining landmarks and the town's classic viewpoint over the canal.
This is where the water-town image you've probably seen online starts to make sense: stone bridge, whitewashed houses, narrow waterways, willow trees, and wooden boats moving below.
Expect this area to be considerably busier than the residential lanes, which is totally acceptable.
You don't come here to avoid people completely—you come here for the view.
8-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou, Suzhou Family TourShanghai-Hangzhou-Wuzhen-Suzhou 
4. Stop at Jiangnan First Tea House
The Jiangnan First Tea House
After roughly 1½–2 hours of walking, take a proper break.
The Jiangnan First Tea House (江南第一茶楼) sits beside the water and makes a useful 20–30 minute pause.
Order tea, sit by the canal, and watch the boats rather than rushing straight to the next attraction.
This is one of the moments when Zhujiajiao works best: you stop sightseeing and simply watch the town move around you.
5. Cross Tai'an Bridge and Lang Bridge
Lang Bridge in Zhujiajiao Water Town
Continue toward Tai'an Bridge (泰安桥) and then Lang Bridge (廊桥).
Tai'an Bridge is where you'll find the large characters "朱家角" (Zhujiajiao) painted on a wall—the classic spot that signals you've arrived. 
Lang Bridge is a particularly good photo stop because you can frame the canal, old buildings, stone bridges, and wooden boats in one view.
If photography matters to you, this section is more rewarding than trying to collect every bridge in town.
6. Finish at City God Temple and Daqing Post Office
City God Temple in Zhujiajiao Water Town
The City God Temple (城隍庙) is a small stop rather than a major attraction. Give it 10–15 minutes if you enjoy historic religious architecture and quieter courtyards.
Then continue to Daqing Post Office (大清邮局).
This restored Qing-era post office is an easy final stop. You can buy a postcard, have it stamped with a Zhujiajiao postmark, and continue walking without adding much time to your route.
Should You Take a Boat: Treat It as an Add-On, Not a Must
Taking a boat tour at Zhujiajiao Water Town
Our recommendation:
Solo/couple: Walk first; add a boat only if the water experience is important to you.
Family/group of 4–6: A private hand-rowed boat makes more sense.
Already/plan to visit Suzhou/Hangzhou/Guilin: The walking route may give you more variety than another short water-town boat ride.
The boat ride is not a bad experience. It is simply not essential for everyone.
The current official hand-rowed boat routes cost ¥200–300 per boat, with a maximum of 6 passengers, and take about 15–20 minutes.
For a family or group of up to six, the price becomes much easier to justify because you are paying by boat rather than per person.
For a solo traveler or couple, it is a different calculation. It depends on whether you want to charter the boat alone or share it with others.

title: Top Things to Do in Shanghai: Beyond the Landmarks
text:
Home

Top Things to Do in Shanghai: Beyond the Landmarks
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Aug. 6, 2026 
For first-time visitors, if you only have two or three days in Shanghai, don't try to fit in every famous attraction, but know which experiences are actually worth your time.
Instead of planning Shanghai by the number of places you visit, plan it by experiencing the city's different faces.
Imagine yourself walking through streets shaped by history, tasting flavors that have been part of the city for generations, and ending the day watching the lights from the famous Pudong Skyline.
These moments show why Shanghai is not just another modern metropolis, but one of the most memorable stops on a China journey.
This guide is organised by experiences rather than by attraction popularity, helping you balance Shanghai's historic charm, local life, and futuristic energy without wasting hours on places that may not match your expectations.
What's Actually Worth Your Time in Shanghai
Top Things to Do in Shanghai
How to Prioritize If You Have 1, 2, or 3 Days
FAQs
How to Decide What's Actually Worth Your Time in Shanghai
Shanghai has more attractions and experiences than you could possibly fit into one trip. 
If your time is limited, don't try to check off every famous landmark. Instead, prioritize experiences that help you understand what makes Shanghai unique.
We believe the three experiences most worth your time are its history, its everyday life, and its vision of the future. Together, they show you where Shanghai came from, how it lives today, and where it is heading next.
1. Step Into Shanghai's History, Not Just Its Landmarks
The Bund at night
Shanghai's historic neighborhoods are worth your time because they show you how the city's past still shapes its modern identity. 
Instead of simply ticking off historic buildings as sightseeing stops, walk through neighborhoods where the past is still part of everyday life. 
Old residences sit alongside cafés, local shops, and modern businesses, giving you a chance to experience how Shanghai has evolved without leaving its history behind.
2. Experience How Shanghai Actually Lives
Shanghai local farmers market
To truly experience Shanghai, you don't travel all this way to see how it performs for tourists, but to delve into the city locals actually live in. 
From food and morning markets to neighborhood streets and ordinary daily routines, these experiences help you understand the rhythm, character, and energy of Shanghai in a way that famous attractions alone cannot.
What makes its neighborhoods so special is that none of them feels preserved for tourists; it simply feels lived in.
3. See Shanghai's Leap from Past to Future
Pick up a food delivery brought by a drone.
Shanghai's skyline is worth your time because few places make the city's transformation so visible, both from above and on the river. 
In a single view, you can see the contrast between its historic roots and its futuristic ambitions, giving you a sense of how dramatically the city has changed and how fast it is moving forward.
7-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
Top Things to Do in Shanghai (Ranked by Experience Value)
Instead of ranking these experiences by how famous the landmarks are, we have ordered them by something more meaningful: the depth of what you actually take away to carry home from each one.
But if you have to pick just two or three, start at the top and work your way down.
1. Walk Along the Bund: See Shanghai's Past and Future Face Each Other
The famous Shanghai skyline
If there is one single spot that justifies the phrase "Shanghai," it is the Bund.  
To get the full effect, the skyline is at its best between 6 PM and 8 PM, when the fading daylight softens the horizon and the new towers begin to sparkle one by one.
Evening is when you will witness the entire riverbank transform into a glowing runway, and the "wow" will remind you why this spot tops our list. But if you want fewer crowds, arrive 30–40 minutes before sunset and stay until the lights come on.
For those who want to explore the Bund in-depth, we recommend a walking tour by day. 
Our guide will walk you through the history of the row of buildings that blend European and Chinese architectural styles and how they survived the war, such as Astor House Hotel, Peace Hotel, and the former HSBC Building.
We are not trying to give you a history lesson, but a chance to see that Shanghai did not erase its past to become modern: it simply built the new by rooting around the old.
If you want to see more aspects of the Bund besides the classic one, combine your Bund walk with a stroll through Waibaidu Bridge to North Bund Green Land, where you find significantly fewer people, unobstructed skyline views, and rewarding scenery along the way.
2. Explore the Former French Concession: Shanghai's Most Walkable Historic Area
The Former French Concession in Shanghai
For visitors who wonder whether Shanghai is nothing but concrete and glass, the Former French Concession tells a different story.
The Former French Concession is at its most lively on weekday mornings (before 9 AM). You'll see locals buying breakfast, walking dogs, opening neighborhood shops, and daily life unfolding beneath the shade of leafy, towering plane trees over quiet, winding streets.
As you wander, keep your eyes open for the old villas with red ceramic roofs and black iron balconies, where elderly residents play chess on folding tables along the streets.
The narrow lilong lanes lead you to hidden courtyards and the tiny cafés that have set up shop in them. Young white-collar workers can always find these quiet hidden gems, enjoy a serene space sipping coffee while tapping on laptops.
If you'd like to explore these quieter lanes without worrying about navigation, our private walking experience combines local food stops with the neighborhood stories most visitors miss.

3. Taste Shanghai Through Time-Honored Food and Local Flavors
Shanghai Old Restaurant, one of the most famous local cuisine restaurants in Shanghai.
When you start wondering what you should eat in Shanghai, the real question is often: "What will help me understand this city through its flavors?" Embarking on a Shanghai Benbang food adventure may give you the answer.
Our local food walks focus on carefully selected century-old restaurants still loved by Shanghai locals, rather than tourist-only stops. From Dexingguan and Lao Zheng Xing to other historic eateries, you'll taste each restaurant's signature dish and discover the classic flavors that generations of Shanghai diners have enjoyed.
Feel free to inform your tour guide of your dietary restrictions and allergies in advance so they can make further recommendations. 
However, these famed restaurants generally require you to take a number and wait in line, so it's best to arrive as early as possible during peak meal times to minimize the chance of queuing, such as around 11:00 AM or 5:00 PM.

title: Shanghai Weather in February 2027: Enjoy Chinese New Year
text:

Shanghai Weather in February 2027: Enjoy Chinese New Year
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated May. 22, 2026 
February is the last month of Shanghai's winter season, with average temperatures ranging between 3–10°C (37–50°F). 
Alike January, the weather in February is usually overcast and rather chilly. But it's not that cold when it's not raining, with daytime temperatures normally above 7°C (45°F). 
February is rainier than January, averaging 7 days with an average rainfall of 2.2 inches / 56 mm. In 2026, there were 11 rainy days, but they were mostly light rain, rarely mixed with snow.
Is February a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Yu Garden Commercial Street was decorated with colorful lanterns for the Spring Festival.
Being weather-wise, February isn't Shanghai's best month. 
But it offers something no other month can: an authentic Chinese New Year (Spring Festival) atmosphere. Unlike December's Western Christmas feel, February immerses you in traditional red lanterns, temple fairs, fireworks, and family reunions.
If you want to avoid the travel rush but still soak in the festivities, aim for February 13–20, 2027, when the Spring Festival period isn't over (the Lantern Festival on February 20 marks its final day), but the holidays have ended.
Meanwhile, February 5–12, 2027, is a national holiday, when you can expect packed attractions, higher hotel prices, and some shops or restaurants closed as they return to their hometowns.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
What to See and Do in Shanghai in February
The Shanghai City God Temple Fair is brightly decorated during the Spring Festival.
Traveling to Shanghai in February, you will feel that all your activities are given the color of the Spring Festival, enriching your cultural experience. 
Generally speaking, you can visit Yuyuan Garden during the annual Lantern Fair, where thousands of colorful lanterns light up the classical pavilions. You may encounter traditional dragon dances, try sugar paintings with your favourite shapes on, and join locals in writing blessing scrolls or Chinese words.
Areas around the former French Concession are at their most lovely because the quieter streets, old European-style buildings, and neighborhood cafés naturally fit the slower season, perfect for slow city walks.
Indoor attractions also become much more valuable during this season. Museums, art galleries, and observation decks on the skyscrapers provide comfortable breaks from the cold while still allowing you to experience the city's culture and skyline.
For a modern twist, you can take your family to Shanghai Disneyland, which also celebrates Spring Festival with characters wearing red tangzhuang (traditional Chinese clothes in the Tang dynasty), special parades, and Spring Festival-themed activities.
4-Day Shanghai Family Disneyland Tour 
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in February
The word "欢喜" (huānxǐ) means happiness when read from left to right, and like/love when read from right to left.
February is cold and damp, but not extreme.
Layer up your outfit with a thermal base, a sweater or fleece, and a waterproof coat. A scarf, gloves, and a warm hat are essential, especially if you plan to be outdoors for temple fairs or lantern viewings by night. 
Comfortable, water-resistant shoes are a must, since rain can be more common in February. Don't forget to bring a sturdy, packable umbrella and a small backpack to shed layers when you go inside heated museums or malls.

title: Shanghai Weather in June 2026: Plum Rain with Rising Heat
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Shanghai Weather in June 2026: Plum Rain with Rising Heat
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated May. 15, 2026 
June is the rainiest month in Shanghai, averaging 12 rainy days, with a peak of 22 in 2025. It coincides with the plum rain season, which means several days of damp and rainy weather could be expected.
As the coolest month of Shanghai's summer season, June's average temperatures range from 21–27°C (70–81°F). However, daytime highs have often reached 30°C (86°F) in recent years, and by late June, spikes of 38°C (100°F) are possible (as seen on June 27, 2025).
Is June a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Our clients had a great time on the Bund
So, is June a good time? It depends. 
For flexible travelers, if you don't mind occasional downpours and want to beat the scorching heat and massive crowds of July and August, early June can be your best shot. 
The first two weeks are generally better, having less rain and temperatures are still bearable. By late June, summer heat and humidity arrive early. 
However, compared to spring (from March to May), which is milder and drier, June is clearly a riskier choice.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
What to See and Do in Shanghai in June
June's weather is unpredictable, so you should plan a mix of indoor and flexible outdoor activities to make up a smooth journey.
Early June (1－10): Best for Outdoor Sightseeing Before the Plum Rains
The Sinan Road in the French Concession of Shanghai
To avoid midday humidity and heat, stroll through the French Concession in early morning or late afternoon. The plane trees here are in full leaf, offering shade, and the occasional rain shower can actually make the streets look more poetic.
Shanghai Disneyland is also at its best, when the weekdays are far less crowded than July or August, and the experience for you and your children will also be greatly enhanced.
4-Day Shanghai Family Disneyland Tour 
Mid- to Late June (11－30): Shift to Indoor Attractions to Ensure a Stable Itinerary
Zhujiajiao Water Town, Shanghai
When the plum rains start to arrive, the Shanghai Museum (East Campus) can be a perfect rainy-day haven, where you can easily spend a whole day exploring a corner of China's millennia-long history by appreciating bronzes, jade, ceramics, and calligraphy.
Yu Garden and classical water towns like Zhujiajiao Water Town are still enjoyable if you go on a dry day. Just remember to check the weather forecast and be ready to duck into a teahouse for some West Lake Longjing if it rains.
What's more, June brings the start of various art and design festivals, so you can keep an eye on the West Bund or M50 art district for indoor galleries and exhibitions hopping.
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in June
June in Shanghai is warm, humid, and rainy. 
You should pack lightweight, breathable fabrics with quick-dry materials, like sport T-shirts, shorts, or light pants, and a few long-sleeved shirts for cooler rainy days.
As for your shoes, comfortable water-resistant sneakers or sandals that can handle puddles are wise, since the plum rains can arrive without warning. But sunscreen, a sun hat, and sunglasses are still useful, especially early June when the sun can be strong between showers.
8-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou, Suzhou Family TourShanghai-Hangzhou-Wuzhen-Suzhou

title: Shanghai Weather in October 2026: Mild, Sunny, Golden Week
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
Shanghai Weather in October 2026: Mild, Sunny, Golden Week
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated May. 8, 2026 
October is one of the best months of the year to visit Shanghai. Sunny days are the norm, with mild temperatures, low humidity, and little rain, making it ideal for outdoor exploration.
Expect average temperatures to range from 16°C (61°F) to 22°C (72°F), with about six rainy days bringing 56 mm (2.2 inches) of precipitation. Evenings are cooler, typically dropping to 13–15°C (55–59°F).
There is no need to worry about typhoons, since the typhoon season is typically over by October, unlike in August, with higher risks.
Is October a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Yes, we always recommend this period to our clients for its generally great weather. But with flexible dates, you can do even better.
Here's an insider tip: October is a month of two halves.
If you want the most reliably mild weather with fewer people, aim for mid-to-late October. For the best balance of comfort and value, this is your clear winner.
Early October (October 1–7) coincides with China's National Day holiday, which is one of the busiest times of the entire year.
Attractions are packed, and hotel rates, flights, and tickets all spike. Based on recent weather patterns, daytime temperatures can still feel like late summer (Shanghai reached 36°C / 97°F on October 6, 2025). Evenings cool down quickly, so layers are essential.
From mid-October through the end of the month, the weather settles into its most comfortable rhythm. Daytime highs hover around 20–22°C (68–72°F), nights are crisp but not cold, and humidity stays low. The crowds have also thinned out after the holiday.
Tips for Traveling During China's National Day Holiday
Normally, we suggest avoiding the Golden Week of October (October 1–7) for a better experience. However, if your travel dates are fixed, these practical tips could be helpful.
1. Book Everything Well in Advance
Don't wait until the last minute for a trip during the Golden Week. Hotels, flights, train tickets, and popular attraction admissions can sell out weeks before the holiday.  
Secure your reservations at least 1 month ahead, and for top spots like Shanghai Disneyland or Yu Garden, book as soon as tickets are released.
2. Travel During October 5–7 for Smaller Crowds
If your schedule allows, start your Shanghai trip on the 5th or 6th for much fewer people. 
The first four days of the holiday (October 1st to 4th) are the most crowded. By October 5th, many tourists from other places begin their return journeys, and Shanghai becomes noticeably quieter.
8-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou, Suzhou Family TourShanghai-Hangzhou-Wuzhen-Suzhou 
3. Avoid Peak Travel Days When Entering or Leaving Shanghai
The worst days for transportation are October 1-2 (arrivals) and October 6-7 (departures). Train stations and airports are overcrowded, and tickets are hardest to get. 
If you must travel on these dates, be sure to book your tickets in advance and allow ample time for check-in and security checks.
4. Swap Overcrowded Landmarks for Alternatives
Instead of struggling through the crowds in Zhujiajiao Water Town, head to Tongli Water Town, which is quieter, more authentic, and also close to Shanghai. 
For history enthusiasts, we suggest avoiding the long lines at the Shanghai Museum (East Branch) and visiting the Aurora Art Museum. The entrance fee is enough to deter a large portion of tourists who only visit free attractions, not to mention the museum's extensive collection of exquisite artifacts, allowing you to quietly appreciate the beauty of art.
If you want to enjoy a skyline view similar to the Bund but avoid crowds, head to the Sinar Mas Plaza on the North Bund, where you can grab a drink and admire the same iconic skyscrapers from a tranquil observation deck.
8-Day Beijing–Xi'an–Shanghai Tour China Golden Triangle
What to See and Do in Shanghai in October
Exhibits at the Aurora Museum
October's mild, dry weather makes almost every regular attraction in Shanghai enjoyable. 
The Bund, the French Concession, Yu Garden, and the water towns of Zhujiajiao or Tongli are all at their best without summer heat or winter chill. It's also a great time for observation decks on skyscrapers like the Shanghai Tower or Oriental Pearl Tower, where visibility is excellent.
And you also should not miss out on Shanghai Disneyland's Halloween season. From early October through the end of the month (October 4 to November 1 in 2025), the park transforms with pumpkin decorations, villains parade with Donald and Daisy Duck after nightfall, and you can meet Judy and Nick dressed in Halloween costumes in Zootopia.
4-Day Shanghai Family Disneyland Tour 
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in October
October in Shanghai brings comfortable mild days and crisp evenings. 
It is usually quite cool, but based on the weather data of 2025, early October can still feel like late summer, especially during the National Day holiday, so bring a few short-sleeved T-shirts and light pants.
Sunscreen and sunglasses are still useful, especially during sunny afternoons. Rain is rare, but a small folding umbrella doesn't hurt.
By mid-to-late October, daytime highs settle around 20–22°C (68–72°F), so pack with long-sleeved shirts and trousers.
Evenings in October are generally cool, sometimes to 13–15°C (55–59°F), so remember to take a mid-layer like a sweater or hoodie, and a windproof jacket with you, especially if you plan to take evening walks along the Bund or a Huangpu River night cruise.
5-Day Shanghai and Hangzhou High Tech Tour 
Visiting Shanghai in October with China Highlights
Shanghai in October offers glorious weather, but the National Day holiday (Oct 1–7) can be overwhelming for even experienced travelers. 
Don't let crowds ruin your trip. China Highlights knows exactly when to book, which attractions to swap, and how to help you enjoy the month's best days.

Top 10 Things to Do in Shanghai
Shanghai, as the largest city in China, has the reputation of “the Paris of the East”. It is not only an economic center but also a famous cultural city with a deep modern urban culture and numerous historical sites. If you want to know about the modern China, Shanghai is a must-see place you need to visit. So what are the top 10 things to do in Shanghai? Where are the most interesting places to visit? Let’s have a look! 
1  
Exotic Building Clusters on the Bund
The Bund of Shanghai is located along the Huangpu River, with a total length of about 1.5 km (0.9 mile) from the Waibaidu Bridge to Nanpu Bridge, which is the most symbolic scenic spot of the city. The Exotic Building Clusters consists of 52 classical buildings of different architecture styles including Gothic, Baroque, Romanesque, Classicism and the Renaissance. These buildings were not from the same designer nor built in the same period, but they do have a unique harmonious beauty. One of the best things to do in Shanghai is to visit these resplendent buildings. You can experience the various art of architecture meanwhile knowing about China in modern times.
 Recommended Tour:  Shanghai 3 Days Tour with the Bund and Huangpu River from $509
2 
Night Cruise along Huangpu River
After seeing the Exotic Building Clusters, cruising along the Huangpu River can be a romantic thing to do in Shanghai at night. In the twilight, the neon lights shine on both sides and reflect each other, traveling on the Huangpu River by ship will give you a profound impression. On the east side, you can see modern skyscrapers. On the west side, you can appreciate the splendid Exotic Building Cluster in the distance. That will be a really unforgettable experience.
 Huangpu River Cruise Booking
3 
Overlooking the City from Shanghai Tower
In Pudong new area, stands the tallest building in China and the second tallest of the world, Shanghai Tower. The total height of the building is 632 meters (2,074 feet). The appearance of the building is spirally upward, symbolizing the shape of Chinese dragon. Standing on the 118-story sightseeing hall, you can have a close look at the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and the World Financial Center while overlooking the whole city. Thus you can understand why it lists on the top 10 things to do in Shanghai.
 Book a Shanghai Tower ticket.
4 
Have Fun in Shanghai Disneyland
Having fun in the Disneyland must be the best thing to do in Shanghai with kids. This is the first Disneyland Park on China’s mainland, which is located in Pudong new area. Here you can experience many "firsts" of the Disneyland including the largest Disney castle, the first pirate theme park and the longest Disney parade route. No matter, children and adults can find the joy in this magic kingdom. In addition, it is recommended to avoid peak hours such as holidays and weekends. If you can only go in these times, probably you will need to join long queues.
 Book Shanghai Disneyland Tickets.
5 
Shopping in Nanjing Road
Another must thing to do in Shanghai is shopping in Nanjing Road. From the West Yan'an Road in the west to the Bund in the east, the Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street lined with different shops stretches around 1,200 meters (1,312 yards). As the most prosperous street in Shanghai, here you can buy  products from all over the world. Besides the famous shopping malls, some classic restaurants of authentic local dishes can also be found. It is really a piece of good news for someone who has a passion for food. Walk to the end of Nanjing Road, you will reach the beautiful Bund.
6 
Yu Garden
Yu Garden is a classical, delicately designed garden with a history of more than 400 years. It’s one of the must-see places in Shanghai. The garden is not far from the Bund and the tranquil and beautiful environment is very attractive. Here you can see pavilions, rockeries and ponds in typical architecture style of South China gardens. Besides, you can appreciate the Chinese calligraphy and inscriptions of past masters. What’s more, Yuyuan Tourist Mart, outside of the garden, is a very busy district with various souvenirs and snacks.
 Recommended Tour:  Shanghai 1 Day Tour to Yu Garden from $109
 Book a Yu Garden Ticket.
7 
Tasting Local Snacks in City God Temple Area
If you are a foodie, then you are welcome to enjoy one of great but cheap things to do in Shanghai in the snack street near the Old City God Temple, which is connected to the Yuyuan Tourist Mart. You can taste nearly all kinds of local snacks here, such as Nanxiang Steamed Stuffed Buns, Chop Rice Cakes, Vegetable Stuffed Buns, Crab-Yellow Pastries and Cream Spiced Beans. And don’t forget the Fried Stuffed Buns, when eaten with Beef Vermicelli Soup, they're really delicious.
 Further Reading:  Top 10 Shanghai Street Food
8 
Tianzifang: Creative Leisure Block
Speaking of free things to do around Shanghai, Tianzifang is a must-see place. It is converted from the unique local Shikumen complex which is a type of traditional residence combining the western and Chinese characteristics. The block is the work base of many litterateurs and artists. There are some unique boutiques such as vintage glasses store and old-fashioned music boxes shop, as well as trendy clothing stores from Hong Kong. In addition, you can find some interesting and creative restaurants here. This place is certainly one of the best places to visit in Shanghai.
9 
Night Life in Hengshan Road
After a busy day's traveling, having a drink in Hengshan Road is one of the definite top things to do in Shanghai at night. As the most widely reputed street of leisure and entertainment in Shanghai, Hengshan Road is famous for the bars of different styles. Relaxing yourself and chatting with your friends here can be really enjoyable. In addition, on both sides of the road there are lush French sycamore trees and the distinctive upscale European buildings in the shade.
 Further Reading:  Shanghai Nightlife
10 
Zhujiajiao Water Town
Zhujiajiao, one of the city's four historic towns, is a definite place to visit near Shanghai. It is a typical ancient water town in the south of the Yangtze River. The town is crisscrossed with various water ways and there are several bridges with different shapes as well as numerous interesting stores. You can choose to stroll around the town on foot or by boat to experience the local customs and appreciate the ancient buildings. By the way, the traditional snacks are also very tasty.

Shanghai Dining: What & Where to Eat
As the locals in Shanghai put it, “Blessed are those born in Shanghai as they have the most chances to taste delicious food”. Shanghai is a multicultural city where people from different regions and with different cultural backgrounds gather, bringing their own culinary traditions. Shanghai dining is not one of the Eight Major Cuisines of China, but rather a fusion of the most appealing aspects of these other national styles of food. The catering industry in Shanghai is thriving, with a wide variety of restaurants to choose from, providing a rich selection of dishes. Additionally, Shanghai people have high standards for food quality and taste, and enjoy fine-tuned cooking. Therefore, it may be safely said that you can enjoy all the best food from home and abroad for all budgets when in Shanghai. What to eat in Shanghai? The following is the detailed information:
Shanghai Cuisine
Shanghai cuisine, also known as Benbang cuisine, is characterized by its rich sauces and spices, fresh and delicate flavors. No matter what dish, it exudes the refined tone of Shanghai people. Here you can find both the rich and savory flavors of Braised Pork in Brown Sauce (Hong Shao Rou), as well as the refined elegance of Steamed Mixed Shreds of Chicken, Ham and Pork (Kou San Si), all of which embody the essence of a well-rounded cuisine. There are also delicious street foods such as Steamed Stuffed Bun (Xiao Long Bao) and Fried Stuffed Bun (Sheng Jian Bao) to savor at any moment. Nanjing Road
China's premier shopping street, the 5.5-km-long (3.4-mile-long) Nanjing Road, starts at the Bund in the east and ends in the west at the junction of Jing'an Temple and West Yan'an Street. Today it is a must-see metropolitan destination attracting thousands of fashion-seeking shoppers from all over the world. Nanjing Road, Shanghai
  Pictures     Video 
As a century-old shopping street in Huangpu District, Shanghai, Nanjing Road was a witness of the city's history. Over time, it has been restructured, undergoing significant changes. Big traditional stores no longer dominate the market since modern shopping malls, specialty stores, theaters, and international hotels have mushroomed on both sides of the street. For shopping convenience, its eastern end has an all-weather pedestrian arcade.
What to Do in Nanjing Road
 Shops along the Nanjing Road  
Exploring traditional department stores and latest fashion stores
Over 600 businesses on the road offer countless famous brands of superior quality and new fashions. Upscale stores include Tiffany, Mont Blanc, Omega, and Dunhill. Approximately a hundred traditional stores and specialty shops provide choice silk goods, jade, embroidery, wool, and clocks. Shopping lovers will immerse themselves in the joy of purchasing here.
Savoring snacks of time-horned brands
Century-old traditional food stores can be easily found on Nanjing Road. You cannot only taste the most authentic Shanghai food here, but also buy some for your friends and families as gifts.
 Top 5 food stores on Nanjing Road:
Zhen Lao Da Fang: Selling smoked fish and moon cakes with meat fillings
Shanghai First Food Hall: Gathering various kinds of local snacks including traditional cakes
Wangjiasha Pastry Shop: Offering wontons, desserts, and special snacks for traditional Chinese festivals
Shen Da Cheng: Mainly making moon cakes with meat fillings
Shao Wan Sheng: Best for its wine cured crabs and mud snails
Taking the Dangdang sightseeing tram
It's an unforgettable experience to take a ride on the old-style Dangdang tram which operates from 8:30 to 22:00 daily. On the slow bus, you can see various stores out of the window, old or new, leaving your view one by one, like the history. A single trip takes about 10 minutes and you need to pay CNY 5 for it. Dangdang Sightseeing Tram  
Appreciating the night view
Flashing neon signs illuminate the magnificent buildings and spangle the night skyline of this lively city. Open-air bars, abstract sculptures, and lingering sounds from street musicians enhance night strolls. Night Views of the Pedestrian Street Charming Night Piece  
Visiting Tips
Shanghai Nanjing Road consists of the East Nanjing Road and West Nanjing Road, divided by the Middle Tibet Road. Comparatively speaking, East Nanjing Road is busier because of its advantageous location adjacent to the Bund, Shanghai's landmark. Visitors can choose to wander along the whole road or just part of it according to physical strength and time.
How to get to Nanjing Road, Shanghai
 To the middle of Nanjing Road
1. Take Metro Line 1, Line 2 or Line 8 and get off at People's Square.
2. Take City Sightseeing Bus Line 1 and get off at Madame Tussauds.
 To East Nanjing Road:
Take Metro Line 2, Line 10, or City Sightseeing Bus Line 1 and get off at East Nanjing Rd. Station.
 To West Nanjing Road:
1. Take Metro Line 2, Line 12 or Line 13 and get off at West Nanjing Rd. Station.
2. Take bus 27, 30, 330, to North Shaanxi Rd. West Nanjing Rd.

Zhujiajiao Water Town
 Located in Qingpu District of Shanghai, Zhujiajiao Water Town, aka Zhujiajiao Water Village, is well-known throughout the country, with a history of more than 1,700 years. Covering an area of 47 square kilometers (11,614 acres), the little fan-shaped town, being regarded as Shanghai’s Venice, glimmers like a bright pearl in the landscape of lakes and mountains.
Endowed with another elegant name – “Pearl Stream” – the Zhujiajiao Ancient Water Town is the best-preserved among the four ancient towns in Shanghai. Unique old bridges across bubbling streams, small rivers shaded by willow trees, and houses with courtyards attached all transport people who have been living amidst the bustle and hustle of the modern big city to a brand-new world full of antiquity, leisure and tranquility. More Pictures Map of Zhujiajiao Water Town (Click to Enlarge)  
Top Activities and Attractions in Zhujiajiao Water Town
Explore Historic BridgesIt is said that to visit Zhujiajiao Water Town without seeing the bridges means that you have not really been to Zhujiajiao at all! Bridges here are distinctive with a long-standing history, built during Ming  (1368-1644) and Qing  (1636-1912) Dynasties. The antique Zhujiajiao Water Town is thoroughly connected by 36 delicate spans in different shapes and styles, from wooden to stone to marble.
Fangsheng Bridge (Setting-fish-free Bridge), built in 1571 by a monk after 15 years of begging for alms, used to be a place where Buddhist monks and pilgrims released aquatic animals at the very beginning. It is the longest, largest and tallest stone bridge in Shanghai region, with five arches. Hence, it has been hailed as “the No.1 Bridge in Shanghai”. On the bridge stands a stone tablet named Dragon Gate Stone, which is engraved with 8 coiling dragons encircling a shining pearl. On top of the bridge are 4 lifelike stone lions. Boats quietly glide through the bridge arches, complemented by the dark tiles and white walls, as well as the carved doors and windows of the ancient buildings on both sides of the river. Together they create harmonious scenes as if you’ve stepped into a dreamy old memory of southern China. It’s absolutely a perfect spot for stunning photos. Sightseeing Boats Fangsheng Bridge 
Lang Bridge (Veranda Bridge) is the only wooden bridge and the most featured span in Zhujiajiao Water Town. The exposed parts of its main structure, including the bridge deck, beams, columns and railings, are all made of wood and retain the traditional mortise-and-tenon craftsmanship. Due to the roof on the bridge with upturned eaves and its elegant and simple style, it resembles a narrow corridor. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing Dynasty (1736-1796), the main streets on both sides of the river here became increasingly prosperous, but people could only travel between the streets by detour, causing inconvenience to trade and daily life. Therefore, the local people built this bridge to connect the two banks of the river, bringing many benefits. On a sunny day, if you’re looking for a cool, shaded spot to enjoy the view of Zhujiajiao Water Town, this is an optimal place.
Ride a Traditional Black-awning BoatComing to Zhujiajiao Water Town, riding the traditional black-awning boat is an unmissable experience. If you are not in a rush, just escape from the bustling crowds elsewhere and sit in the boat, enjoying the gentle breeze and graceful residential buildings on both banks passing by in front of your eyes. There are mainly two options. One is that you can enter the town by taking the boat outside near the Zhujiajiao Metro Station of Line 17, which costs USD 6 per person. The second option is to take a boat tour inside the ancient town. There are three docks located at Kezhi Garden, City God Temple, and North Street. Each boat holds a maximum of 6 people, with a ride duration of 15-20 minutes and a cost of USD 30-45 per boat. You may share the boat with other tourists, which is much more cost-effective.
Stroll Along North Street and Try Local Snacks Narrow Lanes in the Town In the northern part of Zhujiajiao Water Town, there is a quaint and historic street, namely, the North Street, which features representative and elegant ancient buildings from the Ming and Qing Dynasties. Although only about one kilometer (0.62 miles) long, it is the one of the best-preserved ancient streets in Shanghai. The Street is only 3 to 4 meters (3.5 to 13 feet) wide, narrowing to just 2 meters (7 feet) at its narrowest point. The overhanging eaves of the houses on both sides form a unique “sky slit” view. Strolling on this ancient place and appreciating the historic buildings, as well as the many narrow lanes is truly a delightful experience.
Most importantly, the street is lined with long-established stores and exudes pleasant aroma of diversified local food, making it a great place to grab lunch and snacks. Sticky rice dumplings, braised pork, and various pastries made with black sesame and nuts are all worth trying.
Visit Elegant GardensThe ancient water town is also famous for the imposing gardens. The largest manorial one in this region is called Kezhi Garden, whose name stands for two aspects of virtues: cultivating oneself by reading and overcome hardships through agricultural practices. Stepping inside, you can appreciate classical elements of Chinese garden embodied in ponds, rockeries, pavilions, zigzag bridge, tower, etc.  
Next to Kezhi Garden nestles another one—Hexin Garden. It is a relatively quiet small garden, but its interior landscape is truly remarkable, making it an ideal place for you to enjoy the scenery while temporarily escaping from the crowds. The garden houses many antiques from the Ming and Qing dynasties, such as the Rosewood Cabinet with Cloud-and-Dragon Carvings and the Twelve-Panel Huanghuali Screen, allowing you to appreciate the scenery while feeling as if you are visiting a museum. Moreover, the garden frequently hosts opera performances like Kunqu Opera, providing a great delight for tourists who love Chinese opera.
Visit the Great Qing Post OfficeIt is the site of the former Great Qing Post Office established in 1903. The office is a two-story European-style building, with dark-red brick walls and an exquisite mailbox at the front door that has witnessed the development history of Shanghai into a first-class metropolis. The first floor is a free area where you can experience making your own postcards with vintage postmarks and admire various cultural and creative products. The second floor is an exhibition area introducing the postal services of multiple dynasties and displaying precious postcards and original letters in the past.
How to Tour the Zhujiajiao Water Town?Recommended visit time: 3-4 hours City God Temple 
Enter the ancient town from the entrance and follow the river all the way. You can visit the top scenic spots while enjoying snacks and drinks along the path. If you get tired, just choose to relax in the peaceful, slow boat ride.

Best Time to Visit Shanghai
Best Months to Visit Shanghai: March-May; October-NovemberMarch to May and October to November are the best times to visit Shanghai, since they boast cozy and favorable weather, vibrant and colorful scenery, and not very crowded attractions overall. View of the Bund  
March to MayShanghai gets rid of the damp and chilly winter and ushers in spring during this time. Temperatures rise to around 10-25°C (50-75°F), making for a warm and comfortable climate. You can enjoy outdoor sightseeing without bundling up in heavy layers or worrying about intense heat. Moreover, rain won’t pose much of a threat to your trip, as this season typically features light showers and enjoys plenty of sunshine. Furthermore, the city transforms into a veritable world of flowers, with cherry blossoms, tulips, magnolias, rapeseed flowers, and many other blooms filling the streets. 
During these months, as long as you avoid the Qingming Holiday in early April and May Day holiday in early May, you can experience Shanghai at its most romantic with a relatively quiet atmosphere. Zhujiajiao Water Town in Spring  
October to NovemberAt this time of year, Shanghai has completely shed the stifling heat of summer, with temperatures hovering between 15 and 22 degrees Celsius (59-72 degrees Fahrenheit) - an extremely comfortable range. Besides, both the rainy season and typhoon season have ended, and this period has minimal rainfall, dry air, and excellent visibility, making it ideal for all kinds of outdoor activities. Moreover, Shanghai offers a unique natural spectacle during this season: autumn foliage. With these golden leaves, attractions like the Yu Garden and Zhujiajiao Water Town become even more appealing.
Apart from the National Day holiday in early October, visitor numbers in Shanghai remain not very high during the rest of this period. Yu Garden in Early October  
Best Months to Enjoy a Quiet and Cheap Trip: December-February, Except the New Year and Chinese New Year Period 
These three winter months mark the slack tourism season of Shanghai. The biggest advantage of the off-season is, of course, that it offers a quieter and more relaxed experience thanks to fewer tourists. Specifically, visiting either the Bund or the Yu Garden during this time, you can enjoy your trip at a leisurely pace and don’t need to make any effort to dodge crowds while taking photos. Additionally, if you choose to visit Shanghai during these months, your overall travel costs will be significantly lower: hotel rates will be discounted, airfares will be cheaper, and attractions like the Yu Garden will offer off-season pricing.
The New Year period in late December, as well as the Chinese New Year Festival period in January or February, are not part of the off-season; on the contrary, these times are very crowded. If you are looking for a quiet trip, be sure to avoid these two periods. 
Note: This period is considered the slack season because the weather in Shanghai is quite cold. Therefore, be sure to pack plenty of warm clothing for your trip and do not stay outdoors too late in chilly evenings. Quiet Disneyland Park in Winter Yuyuan Bazaar with Fewer Tourists  
Not-Recommended Months to Visit Shanghai: Mid-June to Mid-September
First, this is the hot summer, with high temperature above 30°C (86°F) nearly every day, and usually around 35°C (95°F). Combined with high humidity, the weather feels uncomfortably hot. It’s no exaggeration to say that within half an hour of staying outside, you will feel sticky all over.
Second, Shanghai experiences frequent rain during this period. Mid-June through early July marks the city’s plum rainy season, when persistent drizzles and sudden downpours fall from time to time. Your itinerary will be significantly disturbed: outdoor sightseeing will be inconvenient, visibility will be low and the sky will almost always be overcast, and some shows and parades at Disneyland Park may be canceled. From late July to mid-September, Shanghai is likely to be affected by typhoons, which force you to stay indoors.
Furthermore, it’s important to note that Shanghai is packed with tourists in July and August, as this period coincides with China’s summer vacation. Inevitably, travel expenses will also be significantly higher than usual. Crowded Nanjing Road Even in Morning  
OK Months to Visit Shanghai: Early June & Late September
Though early June also belongs to summer, the climate of Shanghai is not very hot. Besides, the city has not entered the rainy season yet. In late September, the weather gradually cools down, and the typhoon season ends. So, these two periods both feature not bad weather conditions. 
The Most Crowded Periods You Should AvoidThe busiest travel periods you are highly recommended to avoid are the three long holidays - the Chinese New Year holiday in January or February, the May Day holiday from May 1 to 5, and the Chinese National Day holiday from October 1 to 7. How crowded will Shanghai be at these times? At popular attractions like the Bund, Nanjing Road, and the Yu Garden, you’ll practically be pushed along by the crowd; meanwhile, you’ll have to wait in line for two to three hours for the most popular items at Disneyland Park. In addition, hotel rates typically rise to two or three times their usual price.
New Year’s Day, Qingming Festival in early April, Dragon Boat Festival around mid-June, and Mid-Autumn Day in mid to late September are also full of visitors, though not as many as the above three holidays.

Shanghai Weather in April
 April is definitely one of the best choices for those who are planning to visit Shanghai. The daytime is warm and pleasant and the nighttime is cool. Sunny moments are common and only some short-term drizzles occur from time to time. As for the natural scenery, the color of spring has splashed every inch of the city and all things are reinvigorated.
Warm Daytime and Cool NighttimeApril, a spring month, boasts quite warm and comfortable daytime. The first a few days may still see the daily high of 15-20 degrees Celsius (59-68 degrees Fahrenheit), but since then, the daily high temperature climbs and ranges from around 20°C (68°F) to 27°C (81°F). Occasionally, the city may even experience a hot midday with the high temperature of 30-33°C (86-91°F).
The daily temperature gap is large in Shanghai in April, and it is usually over 10°C (18°F). More specifically, the daily low is mainly in the range of 10-15°C (50-59°F), and occasionally reaches beyond 15°C (59°F) on the last several days of this month. Therefore, on most nights in Shanghai in April, you will still feel a distinct chill in the air. Cozy Daytime of April  
Frequent but Light and Short-duration RainThe overall precipitation is at a moderate level of 130 mm on average in April. The number of rainy days, which is 15 on average, is one of the largest throughout the year. 
However, actually, the rain won’t produce much inconvenience for your tour. According to the historical records, the rain this month is usually light in intensity and short in duration.
As for the humidity, it averages 69% this month, and the air is a bit damp. Thanks to the pleasant temperature, the relatively high humidity will not cause an uncomfortable feeling. Sunny View of Shanghai in April  
Long Daylight Hours & Strong UV RaysThe early sunrise at around 05:11-05:43 and late sunset at 18:13-18:33 contribute to another favorable weather condition for traveling around: long daytime. In general, the daylight hours stretch from 12.3 to 13.2 from the beginning to the end of the month. There is no need to rush during the sightseeing, even if you have a relatively packed schedule. 
Sunshine hours average 5 this month. You should be especially careful about the strong sunlight. At midday, the UV index can reach as high as 9, and if you are exposed to this sun light for a long time without taking protection measures, your skin may get sunburned easily.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in April
Temperature: 15°C / 59°F
High Temperature: 19°C / 66°F
Low Temperature: 11°C / 52°F
Humidity: 69%
Rainfall: 103 mm
Rainy Days: 15 days
Sunrise: 05:11 ~ 05:43
Sunset: 18:13 ~ 18:33
Air Quality in April
Average AQI: 52
What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in April? Clothes: For the warm daytime, outfits like long-sleeved T-shirts plus sweatpants, short-sleeved T-shirts and shirts plus jeans, and long-sleeved dresses plus thin leggings are all suitable. On some sunny midday hours in late April, even T-shirts plus shorts or skirts are OK to wear. With huge temperature differences between day and night, after sunset, trench coats, leather jackets, or denim jackets are needed.
Shoes: Sneakers, canvas shoes, and loafers are all good choices, as long as they are comfortable enough.
Others: 
1. During sunny daytime, sun-protection items, including sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen, are essential.
2. An umbrella should be put into your bag for possible rain.
3. This month is the pollen season, and those with rhinitis are recommended to prepare some masks.
What to See When Visiting Shanghai in April?In warm April with many sunny hours, you will find it a very pleasant experience whether you are visiting the Yu Garden to admire the traditional Chinese garden architecture, heading to the Bund to take in the night views, or strolling down Nanjing Road to experience the bustling view of Shanghai. In addition, following special highlights in April may deliver you more choices and a richer experience. Dazzling Night View  
1. Lively Festivals(1) Longhua Temple Fair
Each year, the temple fair is held on the 3rd day of the 3rd lunar month, which is usually in April. During the temple fair, folk performances can be admired, souvenirs can be bought in the cultural and creative products market, and delicious local food can be tasted. In 2027, it will take place on April 9 of the Gregorian calendar.
(2) Formula 1 Chinese Grand Prix
It has been held at the Shanghai International Circuit since 2004 and is a key Asian stop on the F1 calendar. It is typically held in April each year. If you’re a motorsports fan, this is definitely an event you won’t want to miss.
2. Vibrant Spring ViewIn April, Shanghai looks like a giant garden. You will find charming spring views in Yu Garden, Zhujiajiao Water Town, Century Park, the Shanghai Botanical Garden, People’s Park, Jing’an Sculpture Park, etc., which are all bursting with colorful flowers and lush green trees. 
 Street View of Shanghai in April Spring View of the Yu Garden 
Is Shanghai Crowded in April?April indeed sees a growing number of visitors due to the overall pleasant weather of Shanghai and beautiful scenery. Accordingly, famous attractions like the Yuyuan Garden and the Bund will be a little crowded, and hotel prices will grow by much.
Pay special attention to the fact that the first and last a few days of the month will be much more crowded than usual: The Qingming Festival falls on April 4 or 5, and a three-day public holiday is given; and at the end of April, many Chinese will be arriving in Shanghai to start their May Day holiday.
Tips for Shanghai Trips in April1. For trips to Shanghai this month with many tourists, early booking, for both attractions and hotels, is the top priority, especially if your traveling dates are in early or late April, two periods that are actually advised to avoid. 
2. The climate of Shanghai in April is kind of changeable, so remember to check the weather forecast from time to time. On rainy days, you are advised to adjust your itinerary flexibly and add some indoor activities like visiting the Shanghai Museum and the Shanghai Science and Technology Museum, and hang around in malls.

Shanghai Weather in August
 With high temperature and humidity, the weather of Shanghai in August is unbearably sweltering. In terms of rainfall, the city suffers both brief showers and long-duration and heavy rains brought by the typhoon this month. Despite the unfavorable weather, August is a high travel season because it is the summer holiday in China. 
TemperatureAugust is a summer month in Shanghai, and the defining characteristic of the weather is extremely hot.
Throughout the month, daytime temperature hovers around 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit), with the maximum value typically reaching 38-40°C (100-104°F). To make matters worse, the humidity in Shanghai this month stands at 77%, making the air feel even more stifling: sometimes, the weather forecast says a daytime high of around 36-37°C (97-99°F), but in reality, the heat index can feel like around 40°C (104°F). Nighttime temperature generally ranges from 25 to 30°C (77-86°F), which is still far from cool.
In some years, the weather of last a few days of the month gets slightly cooler, with daily highs and lows around 27-33°C (81-91°F) and 23-26°C (73-79°F), respectively.  People Visiting the Yu Garden in Hot August  
RainfallThe rainfall of Shanghai in August remains at a relatively high level of 136 mm on average. During the averagely 11 rainy days, brief showers are more common, which tend to have less influence on your trips. 
What needs your special attention is that Shanghai may suffer typhoons in August. Typhoons may make direct landfall in Shanghai or pass by very closely. Although infrequently, when they do, they bring long-term heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread flight cancellations and the closure of tourist attractions. One or two times, Shanghai may be affected by the outer bands of a typhoon this month. During such times, while winds and rain may come and go intermittently, they will not be very strong and you can still go out and visit indoor attractions. Sunny View of the Bund  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursFrom the beginning to the end of the month, the sunrise time changes from 05:11 to 05:30, and the sunset time changes from 18:50 to 18:19. Accordingly, daylight hours in Shanghai gradually shorten in August, from 13.1 to 12.4. Luckily, they are still long enough for daily exploration, but remember to arrange some indoor visits for the sticky midday hours from 12:00 to 14:00.
The highest UV index reaches 11 this month, signifying that the sunshine is pretty intense. Besides, the sunshine hours reach around 8 per day on average. So, during your Shanghai trips in August, you have a high chance of seeing beautiful Shanghai under bright sunshine and blue and clear sky, but you need to take sun-protection measures.

Temperature: 28°C / 82°F
High Temperature: 32°C / 90°F
Low Temperature: 25°C / 77°F

Rainfall: 136 mm

What to Bring to Survive in Hot and Rainy August? Clothes: There’s no doubt that you need to pack summer clothing such as sleeveless or short-sleeved T-shirts, shorts, and dresses to help you stay cool in the stuffy and hot climate of Shanghai. In addition to this, there are a few other things you should keep in mind:
1. First, it’s best to choose lightweight and breathable ones, such as those made of cotton, linen, or silk. 
2. Second, opt for light-colored clothing, as black ones absorb heat and will make you feel even hotter. 
3. Third, it’s best to pack several sets, since when temperatures reach around 35°C (95°F), your clothes can easily become soaked with sweat. 
4. Fourth, bring a light jacket like a sun-protection jacket in case feeling cold in air-conditioned places. 
Shoes: Choose one or two pairs among comfortable sandals, lightweight mesh sneakers, and slip-on canvas shoes.
Accessories:
1. High-SPF sunscreen, hats, and sunglasses are recommended to protect you against the strong UV rays. An all-weather umbrella is useful on both rainy and sunny days.
2. Consider bringing a portable fan, wet wipes, and a water bottle to help you stay comfortable in the blazing sun.
3. Insect repellent is needed in muggy August. 
Crowds of Shanghai in AugustAugust marks China’s summer vacation, and Shanghai, as a major international metropolis, attracts many family groups, making it even more crowded than usual. Whether you visit Disneyland Park, museums, or the Yu Garden during the daytime or head to the Bund at nighttime, you will find that you are surrounded by throngs of tourists. Additionally, hotel rates will be significantly higher than usual. Crowded Disneyland Park 
Since the summer vacation ends in early September, the number of tourists drops significantly by the end of August.
Tips for Traveling to Shanghai in August 20271. If possible, arrange your trip for late August, when the summer holiday crowds have dispersed and the weather may turn a little bit cooler.
2. Try to avoid weekends and book hotels and tickets for attractions as soon as possible.
3. Early morning and evening are the coolest periods of the day in August, so you are recommended to take full use of them to do some outdoor visits. As for the hottest 12:00-14:00, you’d better do some indoor visits, like exploring the Shanghai Museum. Our Guests at the Shanghai Museum 
4. Pay close attention to the weather forecast to keep informed about whether there is a typhoon during your stay. If there is, be sure to make adjustments promptly.
5. Since there are so many tourists in Shanghai during the summer holiday, some attractions may extend their opening hours. For instance, in 2025, the Shanghai Museum opened some exhibition halls 24 hours from August 11 to 17, and the Shanghai Natural History Museum extended its closing time to 20:00 for the entire month. Besides, Disneyland Park may open till 22:00 on some days in August.
