China Art Museum
China Art Museum, located at No. 205, Shangnan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai was formally opened on October 1, 2012. It was previously the China Pavilion of Expo 2010, and then had been transformed to an international modern-art museum with a lot of brilliant exhibitions as the Shanghai Art Museum moved in.
Shanghai Art Museum was originally located on the North Huangpi Road, No. 325, West Nanjing Road. However, as the area was too limited, less than 6,000 square meters (1.5 acres), thousands of excellent works could not be exhibited for a long time. But now, the new venue is much too larger than the original one. Covering about 39 acres (16 hectares), it is one of the largest museums in Asia. After relocating, the Shanghai Art Museum was renamed China Art Museum.
Twenty-seven exhibition halls are mainly distributed among the 49-meter floor, the 41-meter floor, the 33-meter floor and the 0-meter floor. A top-down visiting route is recommended.
Basic Exhibitions in China Art Museum
The basic exhibitions include four themes: the Origin of Chinese Modern and Contemporary Art, Artworks Featuring Shanghai’s Historical and Cultural Development, the Artworks of Noted Painters and Arts Development in the New Century.
The artworks of "The Origin of the Chinese Modern and Contemporary Art", are arranged in Halls 2, 3, and 6 of the 49-meter floor and Halls 7, 8, 9, and 10 of the 41-meter floor.  They were mainly created in modern Shanghai. About 1,200 pieces of delicate artworks, including Chinese paintings, oil paintings, prints, sculptures, and calligraphy are on display. This themed exhibition is the first one focusing on the history of art of Shanghai and China.
The second themed show is called "The Exhibition of the Achievement of the Project for the Creation of Artworks Featuring Shanghai's Historical and Cultural Development", which is located in Halls 15 and 16 on the 0-meter floor. The artworks in this unit keep a close relationship with the local culture.
Famous paintings of seven noted painters are displayed in Halls 22, 23 and 24 on the 0-meter floor.
The fourth show is displayed in Hall 1 of the 49-meter floor and Halls 20 and 21 of the 0-meter floor, Chinese culture and the beauty of the Chinese landscape are expressed through about 200 paintings and 50 sculptures in this chapter. It is open to the public for one year from October 1, 2012 to September 30, 2013.
Classical Collections
Apart from the four basic exhibitions, there are two excellent paintings in China Art Museum. The highlight of the museum collections - the painting "Immortals Toasting the Birthday of Heavenly Queen Mother" - is exhibited in Hall 4, of the 49-meter floor. It is a representative work of Ren Bonian, a famous Chinese painter in the late Qing Dynasty (1644 - 1911). The painting describes the lively scene at a birthday party. Forty-six figures as well as trees, birds, stones and other characters are well proportionately arranged on the painting. In order to protect the treasure, this painting is covered by glass and visitors are required to stand on the conveyor belt to appreciate this treasure without stopping in front of it. Those who are eager to get a close look can pass the conveyor belt again or see a replica in red and white colors outside the hall.
The other famous collection is the moving multi-media "Riverside Scene at Qingming Festival". It used to strike the audience's eyes during the Shanghai Expo and now it is stored in Hall 5 of the 49-meter floor. This modern electronic picture is 30 times larger than the original one created by the famous artist Zhang Zeduan of the Northern Song Dynasty (960 - 1127). It vividly depicts the prosperous city life in ancient China.  More than 1,000 figures appear in the day and night scenes.
How to get to the China Art Museum
 By metro:
1. Take Line 8 and get off at Zhonghua Yishugong (China Art Museum) Station.
2. Take Line 7 and get off at Yuntailu Station. Take exit 6 and walk north for about 700 meters (770 yards).
 By bus:
1. Take bus no. 83, 177, 1049 and get off at Shangnan Rd. Guozhan Rd. Station, then walk northward for 300 meters (330 yards) to find the museum.
2. Take City Sightseeing Bus Line 3 to get to the museum directly.

Shanghai Long Museum
 The Shanghai Long Museum is a private art museum with considerable scale and collection strength founded by Chinese collectors Liu Yiqian and Wang Wei. At present, it has two large-scale venues in Pudong New District and Xuhui District, respectively Long Museum Pu Dong and Long Museum West Bund. There is also a Long Museum setting in Chongqing.
Long Museum Pu Dong
Located at No. 210, Lane 2255, Luoshan Road, Pudong New District, Shanghai Long Museum Pu Dong has various collections of traditional Chinese art, modern and contemporary art, and Chinese revolutionary art. The light gray white square museum covers a total building area of about 10,000 square meters (2.47 acres) and is divided into three floors.
The first floor mainly displays contemporary art and is equipped with an art shop, a café, a deposit center and a ticket office. The second floor is the permanent exhibition area for revolutionary art which systematically shows the whole picture of Chinese revolutionary theme artworks from the course of the Sino-Japanese War in Yan'an to the new period of Chinese reform and opening up. The third floor is for the permanent and temporary exhibition of Chinese traditional art.  
Long Museum West Bund
Located at No. 3398 Longteng Avenue, Xuhui District, the Shanghai Long Museum West Bund has a total construction area of about 33,000 square meters (8 acres) and an exhibition area of 16,000 square meters (4 acres). Built on the former coal transportation dock base, the museum has a large open space and is characterized by a unique umbrella arch structure, retaining the cool original industrial style. It is separated into four floors. The first floor and the second floor are the exhibition spaces of paintings, sculptures, installations and new media. The white rectangular exhibition hall on the ground floor is a permanent exhibition space for Chinese ancient art treasures like calligraphy works, paintings, and artworks during the Republic of China.
The museum also accommodates more public spaces, such as a restaurant with a river view, public landscaped courtyards, cafes, and art product stores on the first floor and the second floor. There is a children’s showroom, a library, an art restoration room and an art bookstore on the first basement level.
About the Exhibition
Visitors can check the specific exhibition information on the official website. The museum mainly displays selected works of famous Chinese and foreign painters and artists, such as landscape painting, abstract painting, oil painting, sculpture and many private collections of the founders. Many special exhibitions with different themes such as New Year's special exhibition and the exhibitions of artists' works will also be organized.
At present, there is only one permanent exhibition - Asian Impression: Chinese, Japanese and South Korean Contemporary Art Exhibition. More than 40 works from Asia at the beginning of this century are selected. Another highlight of the Shanghai Long Museum West Bund is a beautiful cherry forest nearby. Watching exhibitions, taking pictures outside the museum, and strolling around the cherry blossoms all offer a wonderful experience.
Classical Collections
The founders’ classical collections are on display in the two museums but many in the West Bund. You may appreciate the painting artworks created by famous painters Zhang Daqian and Qi Baishi and a long scroll painting by Emperor Huizong of the Song Dynasty (1082-1135). Ancient Chinese utensils and furniture including a white jade, a rhino horn, red sandalwood and porcelain of the Qing Dynasty (1636 - 1912) can also be enjoyed.

By Metro
Take Metro Line 7 and get off at Huamu Road Station. Get out from Exit 1 and walk east for 15 minutes.
By Bus

Power Station of Art
 The Power Station of Art, the first public modern art museum in mainland China, was opened together with the China Art Museum on October 1, 2012. Standing on the west bank of the Huangpu River, 5 km (3 miles) south from the Bund, the museum spans an area of 42,000 square meters (10 acres) in total. Power Station of Art, or PSA, is the home to Shanghai Biennale and it is a fantastic place for learning about contemporary artworks.
Renovated from a power station, Power Station of Art used to be the Pavilion of Future in the Expo 2010 Shanghai China. The 165-meter (541-foot) tall chimney, which was converted into a huge thermometer in 2010, now serves as the landmark of the museum and an exhibition space. Built three decades ago, the chimney has witnessed the development of modern industry as well as Shanghai's transition from the industrial age to the information era where ordinary people have increasing artistic sensitivity.
The main exhibition hall covers about 15,000 square meters (3.7 acres) and is divided into 12 halls spreading across seven floors. It has stored and displayed Chinese modern artworks since 1980s. The Power Station of Art, which is an open platform for the public to learn about modern arts, is dedicated to dismantling barriers between daily life and highbrow art.
Shanghai BiennaleLaunched in 1996, it is the most influential biennial contemporary art exhibition in China with the longest history, and also one of the most important biennales in Asia. Shanghai Biennale focuses on the interwoven relationship among urban culture, contemporary art and the public. Since 2012, Power Station of Art has become the new home to this international biennale.
13th Shanghai Biennale 2020
Date: 2020.11.10 – 2021.6.27
Theme: Bodies of Water
Description: This biennale is inspired by the COVID-2019 epidemic. During the 8 months, the curators will show audiences that how does water, the spring of life, goes beyond different regions and combines each individuals. At the same time, the biennale is aimed at calling up artists to get rid of individual stance and think about the new form of international connection and collaboration.
12th Shanghai Biennale 2018Date: 2018.11.10 – 2019.3.10
Theme: Proregress - Art in an Age of Historical Ambivalence
Description: The curators deem that contemporary art is a witness of current ambivalence. It reflects disputes and anxieties in contemporary society and help people to adapt to it. This biennale will provide a framework to dig deeply into mankind’s role in society.
11th Shanghai Biennale 2016Date: 2016.11.11 – 2017.3.12
Theme: WHY NOT ASK AGAIN
Description: This theme is inspired by an Indian movie about proposals and refutations, arguments and counter-arguments. The exhibition features a “critical confusion”, interacting visitors with intriguing questions and debates in stories and fables. The 11th Shanghai Biennale provides the public with a thinking matrix of artistry, literature, and philosophy. To appreciate the exhibition, all you need to have is the curiosity and passion for the complexity of life.
10th Shanghai Biennale 2014Date: 2014.11.01 – 2015.5.29
Theme: SOCIAL FACTORY
Description: This year's exhibition centers on the characteristics of "social production" and the components of "social facts". Reviewing the social situation in 1978, a turning point of China's modernization, the 10th Shanghai Biennale aims to explore an array of social questions.
9th Shanghai Biennale 2012Date: 2012.10.02 – 2013.3.31
Theme: REACTIVATION
Description: Given the history of PSA as a power station, the 9th exhibition, also the opening show of PSA, is themed with "Reactivation", which means to regenerate for the contemporary art.
Besides the above-mentioned regular Shanghai Biennale, the exhibitions in the Power Station of Arts always change in order to keep abreast with the times. In the past years, several themed exhibitions have been held. Collections of Centre Pompidou were shown from December 16, 2012 to March 15, 2013.
Tips:It is suggested that visitors rent an audio guide machine for the purpose of learning more about the exhibits, and it is available on the information desk on the 1F. The guide device costs CNY 20 and a deposit of CNY 200 is needed. Or QR code designed by the museum for the exhibits can be used for a guide.

1. Take bus no. 1216 and get off at Miaojianglu Wangdalu Station.
2. Take bus no. 45, 66, 109, 144, 306, 327, 780, 869 or Daqiao Line 6 and get off at Zhongshan Nanlu Nanchezhanlu Station. Then walk south for about 10 minutes.

Take line 4 or line 8 and get off at South Tibet Road Station, get out from Exit 2. Then you need to walk east for about five minutes and turn south at the second crossing. Continue to walk for another five minutes and you can see the entrance of the museum.

Shikumen Residence
 Typical Shikumen Shikumen Residence, literally meaning ‘Stone Warehouse Gate’, is regarded as the most representative house style of Shanghai as the Hutongs and Courtyards are representative of Beijing. It is so named due to the stone door frame. This sort of residence combines the architecture styles of southern China and western countries.
These residences can date back to the 1870s, when the Taiping Rebellion against the domination of the Qing Dynasty (1644 - 1911) broke out. Due to the turbulent warfare, the businessmen, ministers and wealthy people had to move to the concession for protection. As a result, many foreign estate businessmen had a large number of residences built to earn money. Those residences were therefore inspired by western style.
Construction Features of Shikumen Residence
A Shikumen Residence is usually a two-floor building constructed with bricks and wood. On the sloping roof is a dormer window. It has a stone gate frame and wooden doors. Two copper door-knockers echo in the whole lane when they are struck. As the residences are usually linked, a lane naturally comes into being. At the end of the lane, a traditional archway can usually be found.
Stepping through the stone gate, you enter a patio from where the sunshine lights the whole yard. The major rooms are on both sides of the patio. Right in front of the patio, it is a six-meter (about 19 ft) long and four-meter (about 13 ft) wide living room where the hosts meet or treat their guests. Two lateral rooms are on each side, from which you can walk upstairs. Passing through the living room, another patio appears where the cooking bench is set.
The overall framework of the residence is in the architectural style of the courtyards in south China. The indoor furniture and necessity arrangement are also designed based on the representative architectural style. While from the outside, the block of residences looks like western-style townhouses. Moreover, the lintel was usually constructed with Chinese traditional bricks and black tiles. Later, under the influence of western architecture, the doors were gradually decorated with the triangular, circular, arc-shaped or rectangular carvings. Even the outside walls were covered with the western paintings and carvings.
Development 
It’s said that before the 1950s, these residences constituted up to 60% of all the Shanghai dwellings and sheltered 60% of the local population. These typical residences kept the original estate market records of the city. As these houses originated in the concession, they almost monopolized the city’s estate market due to their comfortable, practical and convenient advantages. Apart from these, they were popular because of their good locations, centered distribution and convenient transportation. Such residences were originally built at East Beijing Road, Fuzhou Road, Middle Henan Road and the western surrounding areas. As time passed by, they gradually died out with the pace of the reconstruction of the old areas. Later when some influential architects put forward that these residences should be preserved as a symbol of the typical Shanghai culture, great attention started to be paid to them.
According to official statistics, before 1949, the old residences covered 29.3 sq km (about 11.3 sq mi), including 6.6 sq km (about 2.5 sq mi) of apartments, garden residences and modern lanes and 18.5 sq km (about 7.1 sq mi) old lanes. Even now about 2 million people are still living in these residences, which are mainly seen at Xintiandi, Tianzifang and Jian Ye Li. Such well-preserved residences can also be found at Shang Xian Fang, He He Fang, Yu Yang Li, Rui Hua Fang, Pu Qing Li, Bu Gao Li, Heng Chang Li, Heng Feng Li, Zhang Family Garden and Tilanqiao Area. 
Shikumen Culture
The appearance of these residences broke through the Chinese traditional lifestyle, under which a large extended family lived in a big courtyard. The new smaller-sized courtyard came into being to lay a foundation for the later Lane Culture. Naturally, Ting Zi Jian (a small room in a building), Ke Tang Jian (living room), Tian Jing (patio) and Seventy-two Guest Rooms are all relevant expressions in the Shikumen culture.
This local culture had a great influence on Shanghai’s politics, economy, literature, arts and lifestyle. The literature school of “Ting Zi Jian” was born at the same time. Later the scholars created a large number of masterpieces. Similarly, the architecture also provided abundant opportunities for art creativity so that many movies and music works were made on their background. What’s more, due to their complicated and diverse residences, the local inhabitants formed a distinct lifestyle, which laid a solid foundation for their diverse costumes, dieting habits and life habits.
Shikumen Residence Museum 
The museum not only presents the typical Shanghai architectural style, but also revives the life space and style of the local residents. In fact, it was reconstructed from an old Shikumen house in the 1920s. Covering 514 sq meters (about 614 sq yards), the museum only includes seven rooms – living room, study, senior’s room, landlord’s room, daughter’s room, son’s room and the kitchen. 
The displays in the museums are all about the daily necessities of that time. The cooking range, some textbooks, lipstick and rouge are among them. In addition, the whole setting of the museum depicts the vivid life of a middle-class family. “Wu Li Xiang”, meaning “home”, should be the most representative local expression, whose corresponding expression in English is “Open House”. At that time, “Wu Li Xiang” made the neighborhood closer and more harmonious. Living in the nearby residences, people queued up to use the public kitchens and toilets and chattered with each other as they dried their washing in the yards.

How to get to Shikumen Residence Museum
1. Take metro line 1 and get off at South Huangpi Road Station. Leave from exit 2 and walk south for about 350 m (about 380 yd) to the museum.
2. Take metro line 10 or line 13 and get off at Xintiandi Station. Leave from exit 6 and walk north for about 450 m (490 yd).
3. Take bus 109, 146, 781, 805, 932 or City Sightseeing Bus Line 1 to get there. Location No. 25, Lane 181, Taicang Road, Luwan District Entrance Fee CNY 20 Opening Time Sunday – Thursday: 10:30 – 22:30
 Friday and Saturday: 11:00 – 23:00 
Shikumen Residence Household Museum 
Every Saturday and Sunday, visitors can visit this museum to experience the typical local life. A high fig tree stands in the patio to provide shade on hot summer days. Passing through the patio, you will find the living room, which displays a western and oriental combination style. An old gramophone plays the Blue Danube melody. Then sitting on the sofa, you can look around and experience the locals’ life. “Ting Zi Jian” of the residence is used as a study, where there are “the scholar's four jewels” (writing brush, ink stick, ink sl

Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen
 The Statue of Sun Yat-sen 
The Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen, located at No. 7 Xiangshan Road, Shanghai, is a two-storey European-style building. It may not be that noticeable among the nearby high buildings and mansions, but it has won deep reverence and admiration from visitors since it was opened to the public in 1988. Sun Yat-sen, also named Sun Wen, is the great forerunner of the Chinese democratic revolution, the founder of the Republic of China and the respected contributor to Chinese modern history.
From 1918 to 1925, Mr. Sun Yat-sen and his wife, Mrs. Soong Ching Ling lived in the Former Residence, which was donated by some patriotic overseas Canadian Chinese, in support of the Chinese revolution. It was at the Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen that he accomplished the renowned masterpieces such as Doctrines of Sun Wen, Plans of China's Development, etc., made the plan of reforming the Three Principles of the People (Nationalism, Democracy and the People's Livelihood) and put forward the three cardinal policies (alliance with Soviet Russia, cooperation with the Communists and assistance to the workers' and peasants' movements). It was also here that he received the representatives of the Communist Party of China and promoted the first cooperation between the two major parties in Chinese modern history (the Nationalist Party and the Communist Party).
The residence witnessed his enthusiasm and his contributions to the Chinese revolution during the last years of this great man. After his death in 1925, Mrs. Soong continued to live here until 1937 when the Japanese army occupied Shanghai. Eight years later, upon China winning the war, Mrs. Soong offered to provide her home as the permanent site to Mr. Sun's memory. In 1961, the Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen was listed as being one of the Key State-preserved Cultural Relic Units.
According to Mrs. Soong's memories, the furnishings, most of which were those used by the couple, are displayed where they were. While walking through the house, one can recreate the life of the owners through every exhibited article, either the knives hanging over the fireplace, or the photos on the wall of the living-room, or the books lining the bookcases, or even a pair of glasses once used. The activities of Mr. Sun Yat-sen, especially those of the days when he lived in Shanghai, are also displayed in historical materials and pictures. On the anniversaries of Mr. Sun Yat-sen's birth (Nov. 12) and his death (Mar. 12), flowers are presented this great man with respect from the municipal government of Shanghai, the relatives of Mr. Sun, and people from all walks of life.
How to get to the Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen, Shanghai By Metro:
1. Take line 13 and get off at Middle Huaihai Road Station. Get out from exit 1 and walk south along Sinan Road for about five minutes. Then you can see the site on your left.
2. Take line 10 and get off at Xintiandi Station. Get out from Exit 6 and walk westward 10 minutes to the south gate of Fuxing Park. The Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen is next to the west gate of the park.
 By Bus:
1. Take bus 24, 41, 301, or 986 and get off at Ruijinerlu Fuxingzhonglu Station. Walk east along Xiangshan Road for about three minutes to the residence.
2. Take bus 36, 780, 781, 786, 869, 932, 933, 974, or 986 and get off at Chongqingnanlu Fuxingzhonglu Station.
 Admission Fee CNY 20
 Children under 1.3 meters (4.3 feet) enjoy free entry. Audio Guide Service (English/Japanese ) CNY 20 (deposit: CNY 200 with passport or CNY 400 without passport) Opening Hours 09:00-16:30

Sinan Road
 Sinan Road is one of the best old streets in Shanghai to escape from the bustling city, with western style villas, small delicate shops and restaurants, in the shade of tall plane trees. It joins Huaihai Road to Taikang Road in the Former French Concession. Sinan Road was built in 1914 and named ‘Rue Massenet’ by the French Concession authorities to commemorate the famous French musician who died on August 13, 1912.
One of the Best Old Streets in ShanghaiExquisite houses and tall plane trees edge both sides of the road. In addition to the common road features in the Former French Concession, Sinan Road has more than 20 various old Shanghai style garden houses which makes it a unique attraction. Besides, Sinan Road does not have buses nor neon signboards. The street lights are old-fashioned. All of these make Sinan Road one of the best and most beautiful old streets in Shanghai.    
A Great Deal of Former Residences of CelebritiesThose garden houses used to be residences for celebrities. Former Chinese premier Zhou Enlai has lived at No. 73 Sinan Road, which is a Spanish-style garden house. Moreover, Chinese Peking opera artist Mei Langfang and Chinese modern democratic revolutionaries Sun Yat-sen and his wife Soong Ching-ling also have lived in Sinan Road. These residences are still well preserved and can be visited.  
Sinan Mansions - A Nice Leisure and Entertainment PlaceSinan Mansions are not one building, but buildings of 51 historic garden houses. They also bring together a variety of architectural styles. There are boutique hotels, apartment hotels and enterprise mansions. Moreover, there are a variety of restaurants, bars, coffee houses, tea houses, as well as a large number of clubs, convention centers, showrooms, cultural salons,  designer shops and recreational parks. Whether you are going shopping, enjoying deicious food, staying overnight or appreciating European style architecture, Sinan Mansions can cater to your needs.

2. Take metro line 13 and get off at Huaihai Middle Road Station, leave from exit 1 and walk about 100 meters ( 110 yards) to the east.

4. Take metro line 1 and get off at South Shaanxi Road Station, leave from exit 4 and walk about 500 meters (550 yards) to the east.
5. Take metro line 12 and get off at South Shaanxi Road Station, leave from exit 8 and walk about 900 meters (1000 yards) to the east.
6. Take bus line 26, 42, 167, 198, 320, 911, 920 and 926 and get off at Huaihai Middle Road Station.

Thames Town, Shanghai
 Located in the core area of Songjiang New City, Songjiang District, Thames Town is a large British style community. It is about 41 kilometers (25 miles) from central Shanghai. The town covers a total area of about 1,000,000 square meters (247 acres), with a total construction area of 500,000 square meters (124 acres). In recent years, more and more visitors flock to the town for relaxation, taking photos, or attending various exhibitions and activities.
When visiting the Thames Town Shanghai, you can't help but be attracted by the beautiful and dreamy town where streets, squares, houses, sculptures, streetlights and signboards just remind you of Britain. At the heart of town is a commercial area with many shops, restaurants, galleries, bars, cafés and wedding dress shops. The north, south and west of the town's commercial area are residential areas not open to tourists. To the east of the business district is a scenic lake where you can take a yacht ride or paddle around the lake.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do
Catholic Church
The Catholic Church is the landmark building of the Thames Town. With the largest area, it’s one of the most beautiful spots of the town. Its appearance is like an English castle and characterized by the Baroque style. Surrounded by green spaces on three sides, the main body of the church has three spires, all of which have cross symbols. And the painted glasses of the church are extremely fancy under the sunshine. The church also attracts many new couples to take photos. It should be noted that the church closes early, so it is recommended to first hit when you visit the Thames Town Songjiang.
Zhongshuge Bookshop – One of the Most Beautiful Bookstores in China
Visitors to Thames Town Shanghai cannot miss the Zhongshuge Bookshop, one of the most famous shops in China for its exquisite layout and well-designed bookshelves. This English-style building with jujube red exterior wall perfectly integrates into the street view. Its glass curtain wall is painted with selected passages from classic books from all over the world. Once you enter this bookstore, you will be impressed by the books on the wall, the glass ground and even the glass ceiling. But the books on the ceiling are fake, just for decoration. The bookshop has two floors. The first floor is divided into nine rooms according to different themes. The second floor is full of curved white bookshelves. The ceiling is mirror-like, so is the backboard of the bookshelf, making people seem to fall into the sea of books. There are afternoon tea areas on the first and second floors. Sitting by the window, you can see the street view of Thames Town.
Songjiang Art Museum
The simple and elegant Songjiang Art Museum has three floors. In addition to a few geometric chairs with a strong sense of design for visitors to rest, the museum leaves space for artists' works to the maximum extent. The museum is open for free and invites different artists to hold itinerant exhibitions every week, displaying various works from avant-garde abstract oil paintings to traditional calligraphy and landscape paintings. In addition, there is a film salon on weekends. Most of the low-budget films produced by European directors are shown and people can spend most of the afternoon leisurely here.
Cruise on Huating Lake
Located in the east of Thames Town Songjiang, Huating Lake is a beautiful artificial lake with an area of 200,000 square meters (49 acres). Around the lake, there are houses, hotels, green lawns and viewing platforms. On the west bank of the lake is a wharf with yachts in line. A wonderful yacht cruise can be experienced here. The yacht goes north along the Shengjingtang River, passes Songjiang University Town and finally arrives at the Guangfulin Site of Ancient Culture, offering fancy river views along the way. Grand dragon boat races are held every year on the lake in Dragon Boat Festival, the 5th day of the fifth lunar month.
Sightsee around the Town by Bike, Train
It takes about 2 – 3 hours to walk around the Thames Town. The statues, signposts, red English architecture and shops with different characteristics can be seen along the way. At the same time, there are open-air tea seats, coffee seats and sunshade umbrellas, which can be used for tourists to rest. If interested, you can rent tandem bicycles, bicycles for three and a sightseeing train. The bicycle costs CNY60/hour.
How to get to Thames Town
By Metro:
Take Metro Line 9, and get off at the Songjiang University Town, Exit 1. Walk north about 100m to take the Songjiang Tram Line T2 and get off at the Thames Town West Station. Opposite the station is the Thames Town
By Bus:
Take Songjiang Bus 24, 19, get off at the Wencheng Road Yuhua Road and then walk east for about 3 minutes. Take Songjiang Bus 14, 15, 19, get off at North Sanxin Road New Songjiang Road, and then walk south for 4 minutes.

1933 Old Millfun
1933 Old Millfun, or 1933 Laochangfang in Chinese, or simply 1933, now in Hongkou District, was originally a slaughterhouse, built in the year 1933 at the intersection of Hongkou Port and Shajing Port, not far from the Bund. The architect the slaughterhouse was Balfours, a famous English designer. At that time, it was one of three largest slaughterhouses in the world. Nowadays, it has been transformed into a cluster of creative art precincts and has become the center of Shanghai’s fashion, design, shopping and entertainment. Dramas and fashion shows are often given here.
One of World’s Largest and Most Advanced Slaughterhouse When Built  
1933 Old Millfun, with an area of 31,700 square meters (341,216 square feet), is a reinforced concrete structure. The outer walls are about 50 cm (20 inches) thick, hollow inside. As equipment for temperature control was not available at the time it was built, usage of this construction approach skillfully controlled the interior temperature; even in a hot summer, it is cool inside.
1933 Old Millfun combines eastern and western styles. There is an outer square building with a circular core, based on the Chinese concept “the earth is square and the sky is round”. Viewed as a whole, it is in ancient roman basilica style. 
What to See about the Building 1933 Old Millfun
Lattice Windows
Location: Facade
Lattice windows face west, taking advantage of Shanghai's predominant wind direction and thus allowing for better natural ventilation. The windows also face the western paradise, which was thought to allow a better reincarnation for the slaughtered animals.
Umbellate Columns
Location: between the first floor and the second and a half floor
In the absence of beams, the whole outer building is supported by over 300 columns. The umbrella-like, umbellate caps of the columns are square or octagonal. Visitors can see them along the interior periphery of the square outer building. 
Covered Bridges
Location: the second floor and the second and a half floor
There are altogether four-storey of corridors and 26 sloping, bridging walkways in 1933 Old Millfun, connecting the central circular core with the outer square building. They form special spaces inside the building; together with the mysterious and varied architectural light and shadow, they are popular sites for photography. These covered bridges form a labyrinth, making this building a giant maze. 
Central Atrium
Location: first to third floors
This used to be the site of the main slaughtering floor. The central atrium is connected to the different floors of the outer building by spiral staircases and criss-crossing staircases. The spiral staircases are about one person wide with a graceful arc at a large angle and were designed to help workers escape easily if the animals were frightened and became dangerous.
Sky Theater
Location: the fourth floor
The Sky Theater covers an area of more than 1,500 square meters (1,800 square yards). The center-piece of the 8 meters high Sky Theater, with an area of 600 square meters (720 square yards), is a dome seemingly suspended in midair. It is made of toughened glass, transparent and dazzling. The round dome structure adds visual and spatial impact. The theatre is open only where there is a show, party or other similar activities. 
Things to Do in 1933 Old Millfun
Enjoy Delicious Food
One of the most recommended 1933 Shanghai restaurants is the Niushi Chinese Restaurant, located in Unit 1-203. It is famous for Shanghai and Cantonese dishes made from beef. After the main meal, one can proceed to La Douceur, in unit 1-105, to taste some French style desserts and coffee. Other themed restaurants are worth trying, including Fomula Pilota, themed on Formula One racing, and Canil, where the “waiters” are six cute dogs. 
Go Shopping in Boutique Stores
In Zhenxiangfang Hand Bead String Shop, the designers combine teaism, Tai Chi, Fengshui, and other Chinese culture references into every hand bead string. They also customize hand bead strings based on guests’ wishes. Many other creative clothing, ornament and furniture designers have also opened workshops here. You will find something new and special on each visit.   
1933 Mimi Theater 
Dramas and other kinds of stage shows are given here on an irregular basis. Due to the short distance between the stage and seats, the audience can have a different viewing experience. The theatre is in Unit 1-201. 
1933 Old Millfun Game House
This is a paradise for game lovers. Every visitor is given a private space to indulge their fantasies in the game world. 
How to Get to 1933 Old Millfun
1. Take bus line 854 and get off at Liyang Road - Zhoujiazui Road Station. And walk northward for about 200 meters to get there.
2. Take bus line 25 and get off at Wuzhou Road - Yuhang Road Station; walk northward to the road cross and you will see it. 
3. Take bus line 6, 13, 17, 33, 145, 220, 308, 319, 510, 939, and get off at Zhoujiazui Road - Xinjian Road Station. The building is to your northwest.

Shanghai Century Park
 Map of Shanghai Century Park
 (Click to enlarge) Located on Jinxiu Road in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, Century Park focuses on lawns, woods, and lakes. The park was designed by the British environmental consultancy LUC and was built in four years from 1996 to 2000. It got its name because it is situated at the end of Century Avenue. Its construction was completed in 2000, the starting point of the new century. The park is known as "Holiday Park" because it is both modern and natural. Numerous different facilities are provided for tourists in the park. They can feed pigeons, go fishing, row a boat, peddle a bicycle, or have fun in the green maze.
With an area of 346 acres (140 hectares), Century Park is divided into seven parts, including the Lakeside Scenic Area, the Forest Landscape Area, the Amenity Grass, the Nature Reserve, the Folk Village, the Exotic Zone, and the Mini Golf Course. There are eight entrances in total, and five of them are open to the public: Gate 1 at the end of Century Avenue, Gate 2 at the crossroad of Jinxiu Road and Minsheng Road, Gate 3 at the crossroad of Jinxiu Road and Jinsong Road, Gate 5 at the crossroad of Huamu Road and Fangdian Road, and Gate 7 at the intersection of Huamu Road and Yinghua Road.
Lakeside Scenic AreaThe major things to do in this area include visiting the Century Clock, Mirror Lake, and the Green World Relief Sculpture Wall.
Century ClockIt is a symbolic scenic spot in Century Park. The three hands of the clock are white, and the twelve graduations are made of Chinese little leaf boxes. Beautiful flowers are arranged around the clock, making it colorful and delicate. The Century Clock is controlled from a satellite, with an error of less than 0.03 second. Thus, it is of high artistic, scientific, and practical value.
Mirror LakeLocated in the west of the park, Mirror Lake is the largest artificial lake in Shanghai. The lake covers a total are of 31 acres (12.5 hectares), and is as deep as 16 feet (5 meters). To the east of the lake is a water lock which controls the water level. Mirror Lake is blue and clean, with the blue sky and white clouds reflected in it. That is very charming! Standing on the wharf by the lake, tourists can see the Lujiazui Financial and Trade Zone in the distance.
Green World Relief Sculpture WallIt presents 29 species of animals and plants from the Asian-Pacific Region. It covers a total area of 213 square yards (178 square meters), and measures 87 yards (80 meters) in length. The animals include China pandas, elephants from Thailand, buffalos from Vietnam, Australian kangaroos, American eagles, and Russian bears. The plants, which vary from tropical plants, semi-tropical plants, temperate plants, to frigid ones, show that creatures adapt themselves to the environment.
Forest Landscape AreaThe main attraction here is the Open-air Music Square. It is situated in the west of Century Park. The square covers a total area of 2 acres (8,000 square meters), with a seating capacity of 2,500 people. This is the largest artificial open-air music square in China.
Amenity GrassLocated in the south of the park, the Amenity Grass is characterized by soft green grass, dotted with European-style buildings with red roof tiles. The Spring Garden, Summer Garden, Autumn Garden, and Winter Garden present tourists with the beauty of all the seasons. Additionally, there is a clear stream flowing by. The scenery is quite fascinating!
Nature ReserveIt mainly includes Birds' Island and the Montreal Garden.
Birds' IslandIt is located at the center of Century Park, with an area of 5 acres (2 hectares). More than 100 magpies are bred here. Moreover, there are more than 50 species of trees on the island, such as peach trees, plum blossom trees, and camphor trees. The tranquil island and the lively birds are in perfect harmony with each other. Tourists will relax and delight in the lovely scenery.
Montreal GardenIt is comprised of islands, lakes, exhibition halls, media rooms, and coffee bars, with a total area of 5 acres (2 hectares). The construction of the park was sponsored by the Canadian Government, the Quebec Provincial Government, and the Montreal Municipal Government, hence its name. The garden is intended to show the harmony among men, nature, science and technology, which is cherished by both Chinese and Canadian people.
Folk VillagePassing through Gate 3, tourists will see the Folk Village in the northeast of the park. The white beach by the limpid lake is surrounded with tall palm trees. Broad Ginkgo Avenue leads to the village. On either side of the avenue are exuberant ginkgo trees which are dozens of years old. In a word, the area brims a fresh pure atmosphere, making tourists comfortable and relaxed.
Exotic ZoneThe highlight of the Exotic Zone lies in the Olmec Colossal Head in the southeast of the Century Park. It was presented to the Shanghai Municipal Government by the Veracruz State Government of Mexico. It is a copy of the eighth original Olmec Head of Mexico. As an embodiment of Mexican civilization, the Olmec culture is characterized by its outstanding carving. The head-shaped stone carving is the well-known piece, and features thick lips, big eyes, and a square face. That looks very splendid!
Mini Golf CourseThe Mini Golf Course in the west end of the park takes up a total area of 8.6 acres (3.5 hectares). There are nine holes on the course for golfers to have fun. The course is also equipped with some barriers, including ponds, shrubs, and bunkers. In addition, coffee bars, golf rental shops, bathrooms, and lounge halls can be found nearby. Golf lovers can have a great time here.
Plum Blossom ShowThe park has a long history of hosting the Plum Blossom Show. At the beginning, some potted plum blossoms were displayed in the Montreal Garden Scenic Area during the Chinese New Year (Spring Festival). That was a small-scale exhibition. Nowadays, there are more than 3,000 plum blossom trees in the park. It is the largest plum blossom woods in Shanghai. Local people as well as tourists often come to the park to enjoy the beautiful and fragrant plum blossoms in winter and spring.
How to get to Shanghai Century Park By metro:
1. Take line 2, and get off at the Century Park Station, Exit 1. Enter the park through Gate 7.
2. Take line 2, and get off at the Shanghai Science and Technology Museum, Exit 5. Enter the park through Gate 1.
3. Take line 9, and get off at the Middle Yanggao Road Station, Exit 3. Enter the park through Gate 2.
4. Take line 7, and get off at the Huamu Road Station, Exit 5. Enter the park through Gate 5.
 By bus:
1. Take bus 184, 794, 640, or Pudong 35, get off at the Jinxiulu Shijidadao Station, and enter the park through Gate 1.
2. Take bus Huamu 1, get off at the Fangdianlu Huamulu Station, and enter the park through Gate 5.
3. Take bus 1013, get off at the Century Park Subway Station, walk northward, and enter the park through Gate 7.
 Note: Only Gate 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 are open to tourists.

Shanghai Changfeng Park
 Shanghai Changfeng Park is located at No. 189 Daduhe Road, Putuo District to the west of the city center. With an area of 366,000 square meters (437,732 square yards), it is a large-scale landscape park and a perfect combination of water and mountains. Open to the public since 1959, it is an ideal place for local people and tourists to relax.
There are more than 20 scenic spots in Changfeng Park, including Sliver Hoe Lake, Hill of Iron Arms, Maple Island, Ocean World Park, and the bronze statue of Lei Feng (an example of selflessness and modesty in Chinese culture). Among these scenic spots, Sliver Hoe Lake (Yinchu Lake) and Hill of Iron Arms (Tie Bi Hill) are the "must-see" sights.
Silver Hoe Lake
Sliver Hoe Lake is located in the center of the park. With an area of 13 hectares (33 acres), it is the main area for water activities. Hundreds of willows and poplar trees decorate the lakeside, providing dense shade for visitors to stroll around. Many stone and wooden benches line the lakeside for tourists to rest. Several distinctive fishing ponds, water-lily pools and lotus ponds are located in the southwest portion of the lake. This kind of design embodies Chinese classical gardens. Tourists can appreciate the beauty of the lake and enjoy the peace and quiet as the sun sets. The park also provides many water activities such as speed-boats and fishing. 
Hill of Iron Arms
In the northeast of the park, there is a famous artificial hill – Hill of Iron Arms. With a height of 23 meters (75 feet), this hill was made from canal mud in the past. Embraced by many secondary peaks, the highest peak looks more elegant and peaceful. There is a valley between the main peak and the southeast secondary peak. It is just like an emerald in there. Lots of rare plants and flowers here make it an attractive place for sketching. The landform of Hill of Iron Arms is changeable and uneven. Tourists will see the different shapes of it from different perspectives. Some pavilions are hidden in the hillside. When one arrives at the main peak, they can see the Sliver Hoe Lake and Changfeng Park.
Maple Island
With an area of 2,666 square meters (3,189 square yards), Maple Island is located at the southeast of Sliver Hoe Lake. Lots of red and green maple trees are planted on the island, hence the name Maple Island. In autumn, numerous leaves of the maple trees turn color attracting many local people and tourists. A wooden house with green title copings is another attractive spot on the north of the island. It has 80 square meters (95 square yards) with the height of 2.9 meters (9 feet). To the south of this house, there is a pond which is surrounded by many Malus spectabilis. Birds and rare aquatics attract tourists' eyes.
Changfeng Ocean World Park
Changfeng Ocean World Park, the first ocean theme park in China, is located under Sliver Hoe Lake. It is gaining popularity among children and teenagers and in 2010, together with Shanghai Changfeng Park, received the highest national level scenic spot rating. The main building of this ocean park is located 13 meters (42 feet) under Sliver Hoe Lake. It has more than 300 categories and 15,000 species of fishes and marine animals. Among several exhibition halls, the most popular are the White Whale Show Hall and the aquarium. The White Whale Show Hall is the largest performance hall in China, holding more than 2,000 visitors. Nowadays, the aquarium is the ideal place for children and teenagers to learn science. In addition, it provides some other services, such as undersea weddings, diving and feeding activities.
 Top 3 Shanghai Ocean Parks: Which one to go?
How to get to Changfeng Park Shanghai
 By metro:
Take Line 13 to Daduhe Road Station and leave from exit 1. Then walk to the east along Daduhe Road. Turn south at the first crossing and walk along Nujiang Road to Gate No. 3 of the park. The whole walk takes about 10 minutes.
 By bus:
Take bus 44, 67, 94, 216, 754, 765, 766, 837, 846, 856, 858, 876, 947, or 1227 and get off at Changfeng Park Station.

Dongping National Forest Park
Dongping National Forest Park is in the center of Chongming Island, Shanghai. Covering an area of 1.4 square miles (3.55 square kilometers), it has the largest man-made forest in east China with a forest coverage rate of 90%. Besides the thick forest, dotted lakes, and elegant gardens, there are also many recreational activities, such as grass skiing, rock climbing, forest driving range, and forest sunbath. The barbeque and camping base offer much fun for families and outdoor vacationers, making the park a popular weekend destination.
Swan Lake
 Map of Dongping National Forest Park (Click to Enlarge) 
Entering from Gate No.1 on the south, you will find Swan Lake on your right. There is a shooting range on the south bank, where you can play paintball with your friends. To the east is Baizhu Garden with more than ten species of bamboo, stretching along Yongcui Lake. The garden is divided into several flowerbeds. Bamboos there are all elaborately clipped into different styles, injecting vitality into the garden. 
Dawn Redwood Lake
To the north of the Swan Lake, the Dawn Redwood Lake area contains most of the recreational activities, such as arrow shooting, horseback-riding, kart, bumper car, racing car and grass skiing. In addition to the entertainment facilities, you can also wander in the nearby Maple Garden and Sakura Garden, breathing the sweet air and enjoying the delightful scenery of flamboyant maples and full-blown flowers. 
Bird-watching Terrace
There are plenty of trees in Dongping National Forest Park. Numerous migratory birds come to the park to reproduce all year round except winter. The birds' migration is the most spectacular sight in the park. At the southwest corner of the park, a terrace, equipped with two high-power telescopes, was specially built for visitors on the north bank of Longce Lake to watch this scene. 
Barbeque and Camping Base
You can have a picnic or camp out at the northwest corner of the park. There is a grill zone to the north of Luming Lake, providing visitors fresh ingredients. After eating and drinking, lying on the grass is a good choice to relax. You can spend the night in the camping area enjoying the bright moon and starry sky, if you like. With the chirping of insects around, you will feel truly relaxed. You don't have to bring all your own equipment. There are tents and sleeping bags for rent.
How to get to Dongping National Forest Park
1. Take metro line 6, and get off at Wuzhou Dadao Station. Leave through Exit 2 and walk south. Take bus Shenchong Line 6 at Wuzhou Dadao Metro Station, and get off at South Gate Bus Station of Chongming Island. Then take Nandong Special Bus Line or Nanjiang Special Line, and get off at Forest Park Station.
2. Take metro line 1, and get off at Wenshuilu Station. Leave through Exit 4 and walk west. Take bus Shenchong Line 3 at Wenshuilu Gonghexinlu Station, and get off at South Gate Bus Station of Chongming Island. Then take Nandong Special Bus Line or Nanjiang Special Line to your destination.

Shanghai Zhongshan Park
Located on Changning Road in the Changning District, the Shanghai Zhongshan Park occupies 214,200 square meters (53 acres). Built in 1914, the park first served as the personal garden of James Hogg, a land agent, and was originally named "Jessfield Park". It was renamed "Zhongshan Park" in 1941 in memory of Dr. Sun Yat-sen (Zhongshan is his Chinese name), a pioneer in Chinese democratic revolution. As a famous park in downtown Shanghai, the park combines English-style landscapes with the architectural style of classic Chinese gardens. Inside the park, there are more than 30,000 trees of 260 species. The four dominant flowers are peonies, cherry blossoms, Chinese roses, and sweet osmanthus. Because of the various plants, the air is quite fragrant.
The Shanghai Zhongshan Park is famous for its twelve scenic spots, including the South Gate, the Peony Garden, the Chen Family Pool, the Great Lawn, the Chinese Rose Garden, the Lake of Mandarin Ducks, the Lotus Pond, the Hill and Water Garden, the Big Plane Tree, the White Marble Pavilion, the Great Stone Bridge, and the relic of the rear gate. Among these fascinating scenic spots, the White Marble Pavilion, the Great Lawn, the Big Plane Tree, and the Great Stone Bridge are must-see attractions.
White Marble PavilionThe White Marble Pavilion in Zhongshan Park was moved to the current location in 1935. It was listed as a modern architecture under municipal protection in 1999. The pavilion is square-shaped, with a length of 18 meters (20 yards), a width of 5 meters (5 yards) and a height of 4 meters (13 feet). Built in western classic style, the pavilion includes white pillars, a stone wall, balusters, steps, and stone sculptures. It looks very spectacular and elegant, and the artistic value of the pavilion is beyond price.
Great LawnLocated to the south of the White Marble Pavilion, the Great Lawn is the largest of the six lawns in Zhongshan Park. It covers a total area of 8,000 square meters (2 acres). The lawn is surrounded by the camphor forest, oleander forest, bamboo forest, cedar forest, and ginkgo trees. Tourists can take a deep breath here while lying on the soft grass at their leisure.
Big Plane TreeStanding at the northwestern corner of Zhongshan Park, the Big Plane Tree is more than 130 years old, with a height of about 30 meters (98 feet) and a girth of 5 meters (5 feet). It was recorded in a newspaper that the plane tree was presented to James Hogg by Thomas Hanbury, an Italian knight in 1866. In spite of surviving for 130 years, the old plane tree is very exuberant and strong. Tourists can sit in the shade, relaxed and cool.
Great Stone BridgeBuilt in September 1959, the Great Stone Bridge spans the Chen Family Pool. It measure 4 meters (13 feet) in height and 20 meters (22 yards) in length. To the east of the bridge is the camphor forest, while to the west is a large square. An island at the center of the pool is located to the north of the bridge and the Dongni Mountain Scenic Area is to the south of the bridge.
How to get to Zhongshan Park1. Take Metro Line 2, Line 3 or Line 4 to Zhongshan Park Station.
2. Take bus 13, 20, 54, 67, 88, 96, 316, 330, 519, 737, 765, 776, 825, 941, 946, or 947 to Zhongshan Gongyuan (Zhongshan Park).

Jinjiang Action Park
Located at No. 201 Hongmei Road in Shanghai, Jinjiang Action Park is a modern amusement park, containing about 40 land and water entertainment facilities. Most of them are large-scale recreational facilities, such as Roller Coaster, Awesome Space Traveler, Layered Merry-go-around, Shanghai Ferris Wheel and Canyon Rafting. Jinjiang Action Park was built in 1985, covering an area of 113,000 square meters (28 acres). Every year, more than one million visitors would come there enjoy the wonderful entertainment facilities.
Peak No. 1 Map of Jinjiang Action Park (Click to Enlarge) 
Peak No. 1 is a giant inverted boomerang, manufactured by Vekoma with the one in Jinjiang Amusement Park being the fifth set in the world. The advanced design and high-tech manufacturing technology raise the orbital altitude to 60 meters (197 feet) high and the speed to 80 kilometers (50 miles) per hour. The most incredible thing is that Peak No. 1 combines the plummeting of a space shuttle and high-speed rolling of a roller coaster together, giving visitors multiple excitement on the 734-meter (2,408-foot) track. 
Roller Coaster
Roller Coaster in Jinjiang Action Park is a large forward-backward reciprocating ride. It can carry 24 visitors at a time. The two ends point upwards, which makes it look like a dragon in the air. Sitting in the cabin, visitors will have an amazing feeling of rolling in the sky. What an exciting adventure!
Shanghai Ferris Wheel
Shanghai Ferris Wheel is the first giant Ferris wheel in China that is higher than 100 meters (328 feet). The overall height of it is 108 meters (354 feet) and the diameter is 98 meters (322 feet). It would take about 25 minutes to run a circle. The Ferris wheel contains 42 cabins, and they are all deliberately designed to be unique, colorful and bright. The decoration inside the cabins is roomy and comfortable. Equipped with computer-controlled high power illuminations, it looks like a colorful moon during the night. 
Canyon Rafting
This is an ultra-large overwater entertainment facility in Jinjiang Amusement Park suitable for all ages. Sitting on the raft floating down the river is like travelling among the green hills and rivers in the mountainous region. The flows are alternately gentle and rapid. Peculiar cliffs along the river will definitely attract your eyes. You may see a waterfall hanging on the precipice in front of you during the rafting. 
How to Get to Jinjiang Action Park?
 By Metro
Take Metro Line 1, and get off at Jinjiang Park Station. Then go out via Exit 2 and walk west for about 10 minutes to enter the park from the east gate.
 By Bus
1. Take Bus No. 757, 804, or the Gumei Loop Line, and get off at Hongmei Road-Humin Road Station, and you'll see the east gate of the park immediately.
2. Take Bus No. 122, 166, 703, 704, 712, 747, Shangshi Line, or Xumin Line, and get off at Humin Road-South Hongmei Road. Then walk northwest for 3 minutes to enter the park from the east gate.
3. Take Bus No. 257 and get off at Guijiang Road-Humin Road Station. Walk for 9 minuetes to enter the park from the east gate.

2. Children under 1.4m (4.6 feet) can buy a sightseeing ticket at the cost of CNY 20, but no entertainment facilities are included.

上海外滩旅游指南：看什么、做什么、了解什么
CLI 团队
中文语言与文化专家
 2021 年 12 月 28 日 
 15 分钟阅读 
 30,909 次浏览
 链接已复制！
 目录
 要点速览
 外滩，中文叫作 外滩（Wàitān），是上海沿黄浦江的历史滨水步道，全长约 1.5 公里。
 这里以 52 座保存完好的西式建筑闻名，这些建筑建于 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初。
 江对岸是现代化的陆家嘴天际线，让外滩成为新旧上海交汇的地方。
 这里最值得体验的活动包括沿江漫步、乘船游览黄浦江，以及欣赏海关大楼和旧汇丰银行大楼等地标建筑。
 外滩乘地铁、公交或轮渡都很方便，其中南京东路站最为便捷。
外滩是上海著名的滨水观光步道，是前往这座中国最具活力的大都市的游客必看之地。游览外滩，你可以一窥上海这座世界最大城市之一的历史，以及它在现代的崛起。
 外滩是上海最具标志性的景点之一，它融合了殖民时代的建筑风格和现代都市的滨江风光。
外滩一侧是保存完好的殖民时期建筑，另一侧是充满未来感的天际线，跻身中国最值得一去的地方之列。适合慢慢散步、乘船游览江景，再对每栋建筑背后的故事多一点好奇心。
这里也有丰富的文化与历史体验，如果你想在中国学中文，同时感受真实的语言和文化环境，这里是一个很值得一去的地方。接下来，我们来看看这里能做什么、能看什么，以及怎样玩得更尽兴。
 滩
01 外滩简介
外滩又称外滩（Wàitān），是中国上海一处受保护的历史滨水区域，全长 0.93 英里（1.5 公里）。它沿中山路（中山路 Zhōngshānlù）东段延伸，毗邻黄浦江西岸。
 外滩是亚洲最具标志性的目的地之一。
外滩的历史
殖民时期，西方列强多次试图控制中国，迫使中国开放贸易并允许西方人定居。当时的清朝政府对此加以抵制。
然而，1842 年第一次鸦片战争中败给英国后，中国被迫开放包括上海在内的五个主要港口，允许对外通商。英国人因此获得了在黄浦江沿岸（即今天外滩所在地）定居的权利。
1863 年，英国人与美国人联手设立了公共租界，外滩由此进一步发展。从 19 世纪 60 年代到 20 世纪 30 年代，外滩是整个上海受政府保护程度最高的外国人聚居区。
19 世纪末，外滩沿线建起了英国殖民风格和新古典主义风格的建筑。20 世纪初，又陆续建成多座重要金融机构的办公大楼，其中包括香港上海汇丰银行（HSBC）和中国通商银行。
如今的外滩汇集了众多历史悠久的西式建筑，建筑风格丰富多样。
 外滩的许多历史建筑由居住在上海的英国人和美国人建造。
 名
02 外滩为何闻名？
外滩以 52 栋西式历史建筑闻名，这些建筑建于 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初，包含罗马式、巴洛克式、哥特式、文艺复兴式和新古典主义复兴式等风格的代表作。
其中有曾是亚细亚火油公司办公楼的亚细亚大楼，以及最初为保险公司所在、如今是购物中心的有利大楼。原汇丰银行大楼现为上海浦东发展银行所在地。
外滩上另一处著名建筑是招商银行大楼。总的来说，这 52 栋历史建筑见证了西方殖民影响在这座城市的历史与发展中所起的作用。
如今，这些建筑如同一座活的博物馆，共同构成了中国游客到访量最大的目的地之一。
 观看这段视频，近距离欣赏外滩的历史建筑和江景风光。
 游
03 外滩必做之事
外滩可玩的内容很多。看看下面的清单，了解这条历史名路上最受欢迎的景点和活动吧。
1. 漫步外滩
想欣赏全部 52 座历史建筑之美，最好的方式就是沿着它们所在的 0.93 英里（1.5 公里）滨水步道走一走。大约需要两个半小时，但这也许会是你在上海最难忘的几个小时。
沿着外滩漫步，你可以欣赏这些历久弥新的建筑，同时眺望黄浦江对岸标志性的陆家嘴天际线。这条天际线上有上海一些最著名的建筑，例如上海中心大厦和东方明珠塔。
记得带上水，再备一把伞或一件雨衣，以防天气变化。
 漫步外滩，是感受现代上海的好方法。
2. 畅游黄浦江
如果你不想走两个半小时，可以考虑乘船游览黄浦江。在船上，你能感受外滩历史建筑与陆家嘴现代摩天大楼之间的鲜明对比。
如果想省钱，像本地人一样体验外滩，可以从外滩乘渡轮过黄浦江到浦东。只需 2 元人民币，就能游览江的两岸。
你也可以乘现代游船游览黄浦江，甚至还能享用一顿地道的上海菜。这类游船航程 30–50 分钟，白天和夜晚都有，30 分钟的航程费用约为 150 元（22 美元）。
无论选择渡轮还是豪华游轮，都建议在晚上乘船。天黑后，上海璀璨的灯光会在水面上呈现出最壮丽的景象。
 乘船游览黄浦江，可以欣赏上海许多最令人难忘的建筑。
3. 在黄浦公园放松身心
走了很久或游完江之后，不妨去黄浦公园歇一歇。这片小小的绿洲，是整个上海最宁静的地方之一。
这里的草坪茂盛、养护得当，很适合纳凉、静坐冥想，或者随手拍些美照。
 黄浦公园位于外滩北端，黄浦江与苏州河在此交汇。
4. 看本地人锻炼
外滩沿江的人行道宽阔，本地人都觉得是锻炼的好地方。如果你在黎明或黄昏时来，通常能看到上海居民早晨慢跑，或傍晚打太极（太极拳 tàijí quán）。
你可以在一旁观看，想多消耗点卡路里的话也可以加入。总的来说，在外滩锻炼是体验本地生活方式的一种有趣途径。
 在外滩打太极（太极拳 tàijí quán）是当地人很喜欢的休闲方式。
5. 拍摄全景照片
来外滩，是拍摄上海壮观天际线全景照片的绝佳机会。
站在滨江步道上或乘坐游船游览黄浦江，你都可以拍到对岸标志性建筑的精彩照片，包括上海中心大厦、金茂大厦和上海环球金融中心。
 外滩是拍摄陆家嘴天际线全景照片的最佳地点。
 观
04 外滩必看景点
很多人来外滩只是为了拍照、欣赏历史建筑的外立面。不过，花些时间看看建筑内部，再去逛逛其他景点，会让这趟旅程更加丰富。
请注意，大多数建筑仍在使用中，未必随时对游客开放。不过，外滩许多最具历史意义的建筑，大堂往往可以进去看一看，而且很有意思。
1. 老汇丰银行大楼
汇丰银行旧址（香港上海汇丰银行大楼）是一座六层的新古典主义建筑，约从 1923 年到 1955 年一直是汇丰银行的总部。这座气势恢宏的建筑曾是世界第二大银行大楼、远东最大的银行大楼。
如今，这座位于外滩 12 号的大楼是上海浦东发展银行的所在地。它是一件建筑杰作，对全球化历史感兴趣的人一定会被它吸引。
它最大的看点是建筑设计，入口大厅中央有一座巨大的穹顶。穹顶上装饰着色彩斑斓的马赛克画，描绘了汇丰设有分行的重要贸易城市的风光，包括香港、东京、伦敦、纽约、曼谷、巴黎和加尔各答。
如果你好奇 1923 年前后的曼谷或加尔各答天际线是什么模样，这座大楼应该排在你的行程前列。
 汇丰银行旧址大楼曾是远东最大的银行大楼。
2. 海关大楼
海关大楼是一栋 8 层高的建筑，建于 1927 年。它位于 13 号，紧邻原汇丰银行大楼，以其标志性的钟楼而闻名，该钟楼仿照伦敦的大本钟建造。
有意思的是，海关大楼至今仍作为海关使用。它与汇丰银行旧址大楼一起，被视为外滩乃至整个上海的象征。
 海关大楼的钟楼是外滩最令人难忘的建筑之一。
3. 外滩金融牛（上海牛）
外滩金融牛俗称上海牛，高 3.2 米（10.5 英尺），长约 5.2 米（17 英尺），与华尔街铜牛的尺寸几乎一样。
外滩金融牛由意大利裔美国雕塑家阿图罗·迪·莫迪卡（Arturo Di Modica）创作，象征中国经济的活力。它于 2010 年在全球金融危机刚过之后落成于外滩，寓意上海经济的实力与活力。
 外滩金融牛是现代中国经济实力的象征，游客很可能会联想到纽约华尔街的那头铜牛。
4. 外滩信号台（Gutzlaff Signal Tower）
外滩信号台又称外滩气象塔，是一座高 36.8 米的装饰艺术风格信号台，最初用于为黄浦江提供天气预报和台风警报。虽然几经重建，但最初的信号塔建于 1865 年。
如今，塔内一层是一座介绍外滩历史的博物馆，二层是café。
 参观外滩信号台博物馆，深入了解外滩的历史。
5. 外滩观光隧道
外滩观光隧道是一条水下通道，连接外滩与附近的浦东新区。隧道于 1998 年动工，2000 年投入运营。
自那以后，它一直深受想去黄浦江对岸一探究竟的游客欢迎。隧道之旅中的声光效果一定会让你喜欢。
前往浦东的行程需要 3–5 分钟，可 360 度欣赏周围景象。单程票约 50 元人民币，往返票 70 元，运营时间为早上 8 点至晚上 10 点。
 乘坐外滩观光隧道，体验黄浦江底的绚丽之旅。
6. 和平饭店
和平饭店是外滩最重要、最著名的历史地标之一。这座装饰艺术风格的杰作是老上海的著名标志，曾在多部电影和小说中出现，并接待过无数国际名人。
需要注意的是，和平饭店其实由两栋建筑组成。一栋是斯沃琪和平饭店艺术中心，前身是汇中饭店；另一栋是费尔蒙和平饭店，至今仍是一家豪华酒店。
即使你不打算入住，也不妨在这里的六家精致餐厅之一用餐。一层大部分区域对游客开放，还有一座小型博物馆讲述这座建筑的故事。
 看到绿色屋顶就能认出和平饭店，这屋顶其实是由氧化的铜制成的。

05 游览外滩的最佳时段
游览外滩，一般选在晴朗天气的上午或下午最合适。天气好的时候，隔江远眺陆家嘴，景色最美。
如果想进入一些历史建筑内部参观，建议在工作日的营业时间前往。
 在晴朗的好天气游览外滩，能获得眺望陆家嘴的最佳视野。
 行
06 如何前往外滩
你可以乘公交、轮渡或地铁前往外滩。出发前先学几句中文旅行用语，问路会顺畅得多。
乘公交车
可在中山公园乘坐 133 路或 135 路公交车。
乘轮渡
可从浦东乘轮渡横渡黄浦江。
乘地铁
外滩上没有直接设站的地铁站，但你可以乘坐上海地铁到附近的南京东路站（南京东路站 Nánjīngdōnglù Zhàn）。从 2 号口出站，朝标志性的东方明珠塔方向步行约 10 分钟，就能到达外滩。
 我们推荐乘地铁到南京东路站（南京东路站 Nánjīngdōnglù Zhàn），再向东步行约 10 分钟到达外滩。
 食
07 在外滩吃什么、喝什么
外滩周边有众多精致餐厅和本地小馆。不妨专程安排一次，或顺路走进一家，品尝中国的一些顶级美食。
必尝的菜肴有清蒸蟹、北京烤鸭和红烧肉，可以搭配一碗汤包或一壶中国绿茶。
外滩及附近的许多餐厅价格相当高，如果预算有限，可能要避开它们。
 小龙虾深受上海本地人和游客的喜爱。
 邻
08 周边景点
逛完外滩后，你还可以去附近的几个景点看看。
南京东路（南京东路 Nánjīngdōnglù）
南京东路是上海最繁华的街道，两旁有高端商场、本地小吃店和各大品牌店。
在这里，你既能选购中国传统工艺品，也能挑选现代潮品，500 多家商店提供丰富多样的购物体验。
 南京东路是上海重要的购物目的地，不容错过。
外白渡桥（外白渡桥 Wàibáidù Qiáo）
在外滩附近看日落，没有比外白渡桥更好的地方了。这是一座横跨苏州河、由西方人设计的历史钢桥，英文又称“Garden Bridge”。现在的桥建于 1907 年，是中国目前仅存的驼峰式桁架桥。
站在桥上，可以饱览外滩和整个上海的壮丽景色，这里也是拍摄电视剧和电影的热门地点，甚至还出现在多部中国小说中。
 外白渡桥是上海的地标，经常出现在电视剧和电影中。
豫园（豫园 Yùyuán）
豫园是仿照著名的苏州园林建造的一片绿洲。园内古典中式建筑众多，散布在迷人的池塘、小桥和假山之间，让游客尽情感受。
这座占地 20,000 平方米的园林始建于明代，不用离开上海，就能了解中国传统造园艺术，十分值得一去。游览之后，别忘了顺道去附近的豫园商城，那是一条汇集本地餐厅和工艺品店的著名街道。
 想在上海市中心欣赏中国传统建筑，豫园是个好去处。

10 外滩：上海的过去与未来交汇之处
外滩既有保存完好的西式历史建筑，又能将陆家嘴现代天际线的壮丽景色尽收眼底，堪称这座城市的核心。如果你在上海只有几个小时，就应该把时间花在这里。
外滩位于东西方、过去与未来的交汇点。今天就来探索上海最具标志性的景点之一吧！
游览上海之后，我们建议你再抽出时间去附近的几座城市看看，这样能更全面地了解现代中国。你可以阅读我们为邻近城市撰写的旅行指南，如苏州、杭州和乌镇，帮助你规划行程。
 来外滩走一走，深入了解上海的过去、现在与未来。

 豫园是受《中华人民共和国文物保护法》及《上海市文物保护条例》等法律、法规保护的全国重点文物保护单位。
 为切实保障豫园开放运营平稳有序，让您获得完美的游览体验，敬请每一位游客仔细阅读并知悉下述游览须知：
1请在豫园官方销售渠道购票，避免不必要的经济损失。
2请主动出示真实有效的优抚证件，配合园方售、检票及查验工作。
3请遵守豫园开闭园时间，合理安排您的游览行程，支持配合园方闭园清场工作。
4古典园林内步道不平，台阶、石桥、坡道、池塘、假山、山洞、低矮树杈、苔藓等区域较多，请留意园内各处的安全警示标牌，随时注意游览安全。建议老、弱、病、残、孕、未成年人、醉酒等游客，在监护人陪护下入园参观。
5园内生态环境较好，偶有野生小动物出没，禁止追捉、触碰、喂食和拍照，建议绕行避让，避免发生人身意外伤害事故。
6雨雪天气时，园内步道非常湿滑，避免滑倒受伤；强风、雷暴等恶劣天气时，不要在树下或屋檐下停留，避免坠物或雷击伤害。
7如遇到园内古建筑修缮、园艺养护、部分景点临时封闭时，请根据园方指示的安全通道行走。
8因条件限制，园方暂时无法提供行李寄存服务，请妥善保管好随身物品，避免财物损失。
9豫园适合步行参观，如确需使用儿童推车或轮椅，请随时注意使用安全。
10为保障豫园正常开放运营，任何组织或个人，未经豫园官方备案许可，不得在园内擅自实施设摊、卖艺、兜售、营销宣传、问卷调查、测量测绘、规模写生、规模拍摄（婚纱、航拍、影视、综艺、商业）等行为。
11禁止游客携带宠物入园（导盲犬除外）。
12如遇各类突发事件或紧急情况，可就近寻求园方工作人员帮助。
 感谢您的理解与支持！
 上海豫园管理处

title: 上海迪士尼攻略（6次吐血总结）
text:
上海迪士尼攻略（6次吐血总结）
上海迪士尼攻略（6次吐血总结）
Little X
用心做好每一件小事
4609 赞同
201 评论
1.7 万收藏
最近又去了一次迪斯尼，结合之前五次的经验，做一份最新攻略。
人较少的游玩的时间1月、3月、9月
之前四次去的时间分别是1月初、6月初、9月下旬和万圣节，1月初那次从早到晚都不用排队，6月和9月那两次去的时候排队都比较久，而且天气也比较热，万圣节就跳过不说（这种特殊节日遍地都是人 ），总结按照自己亲身体验：1月比较空，适合游玩。
知乎上看到过一篇关于“一年中上海迪士尼哪一天最空”的文章，里面虽然是2019年的数据，一般在寒暑假结束后的一个月比较空的，2021年的话，应该就是3月和9月。
2021年疫情还没结束，但和2020年相比，防控比较严格，2020年6月去的时候，迪士尼对于疫情防控也做的很好，要求所有在园的游客必须带上口罩，排队也要有1米左右的间隔，安全上有保障，但是相比正常时候，更多游客会在安全的问题上，游玩的积极性肯定没有以前高，所以人不会出现特别多的情况。
最近打算去还有一点，就是关注了这段时间的排队情况，排队时长以5分钟为主，即：不用排队

正常游玩的话，看下面⬇️⬇️⬇️
一天中排队时间，刚开园的半个小时和晚上18点后排队会比较少。
一早就进园的人和对比白天其他时间段，肯定是刚开园的时候人少，大家都知道，各种原因（起床晚、路途远等等）导致开园的时候还有很多人在路上，所以这个时候进园，各个项目都还没有游客，排队自然少。
晚上18点后就是凭自己前三次（1月、6月和9月）的经验，每次18点后项目排队的人都是骤减，基本上白天要排队的项目，这个时候直接走进去玩就行，像雷鸣山漂流、海盗船都是连着玩了3遍。
游玩线路推荐
先看下上海迪士尼的地图，做个大概的了解。从入口进去后走到米奇大街路口：
向右转：探险岛→宝藏湾→梦幻世界→明日世界→奇想花园
向左转：明日世界→梦幻世界→奇想花园→宝藏湾→探险岛
向直走：奇想花园→明日世界→梦幻世界→宝藏湾→探险岛
个人最推荐第1条线路，按照一早开门就进园的话，先去探险岛玩个飞越地平线，白天一天玩下来到明日世界差不多下午五六点，正好玩创极速光轮，这个时间排队的人也比较少，最后晚上到奇想花园看个烟花秀再做个旋转木马，完美~

好玩指数
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 
①翱翔·飞越地平线：从空中进行一场环球之旅，效果做的还不错。
②雷鸣山漂流：旋转的漂流，注意防水很重要，建议自带雨衣，忘记带的千万别吝啬钱包，排队时买一件一次性的雨衣，晚上7点后进场，还能连玩几次，雨衣的钱都值回来啦。
③沉落宝藏之战：是一场有剧情的海盗船之旅，让你身临其境地进入了一场夺宝的电影中，其中从海底回到海平面的效果做的非常逼真，一定要体验下。
④七个小矮人矿山车：是个《白雪公主和七个小矮人》的过山车项目，刺激之余，还能看看旁边的场景，帮你缓解下紧张的氛围。
⑤小飞侠天空奇遇：坐飞船去遨游天际，漫天繁星，是个浪漫又好玩的项目，只是可惜时间有点短，也有可能是太好玩所以时间过得特别快，anyway，至少玩两遍哈。
⑥创极速光轮：坐着“摩托车”高空旋转、翻越，听很多人说，一定要睁开眼睛去感受，放飞自我，but，我从未做到，每次去必玩，每次玩必定闭上眼睛，尖叫已经让我忘记了别人说的话， 
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 
①探险家独木舟：身高应该没有要求（官网上没看到写），但学龄前儿童不在范围内，是一个手动划船项目，是的，整艘船大家一起自己划船，注意安全就行。
②古迹探索营：是一个惊险的神索挑战项目，用惊险是本人胆子小，好几个地方都是感觉脚抖会摔下去，不过里面还会分难度，像我们这种胆子小的，可以选择难度小的走，克服心理障碍，安全通过没有问题，胆子大的可以选择难度高的，什么体验我就不好说了，毕竟我是胆子小的没走过……
③小熊维尼历险记：布景很漂亮、很卡通，小朋友会非常喜欢，大孩子们如果喜欢小熊维尼的，可以带你回忆下维尼和它的朋友们。
④旋转疯蜜罐：非常适合拍照的场景，属于怎么拍都漂亮的。如同这个项目的名称，坐在一个蜂蜜罐中，旋转、旋转、旋转，从头到底的旋转，建议游玩前不要吃太饱……
⑤喷气背包飞行器：总结为可以飞的高科技旋转木马，握手的地方有按钮可以操控高度，高度任凭你喜欢，很不错哦~
⑥旋转木马：这是大家熟知的项目，最美的莫过于天全黑后，闪闪亮的木马给人的梦幻感觉，真是一个求婚的好地方呢……
⭐️⭐️⭐️ 
①爱丽丝梦游仙境迷宫：一个漂亮又疯狂的大迷宫，不赶时间的可以好好拍照。
②巴斯光年星际营救：小朋友会很喜欢，拿着手枪打怪兽，但去年一天连玩4次后，我对他的兴趣度已经减弱，如果换做以前，可以给到4颗星，sorry~
③漫游童话时光：是白雪公主的童话世界，在城堡中感受这位迪士尼公主的故事。
④小飞象：这个是可以飞的旋转木象，造型非常好看，但因为大多数游乐场所都有，所以只给了3颗星，sorry~ 
PS：好玩指数为个人总结，仅供参考！
演出推荐
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 
《夜光幻影秀》绝对不能错过的烟花表演，上海的烟花表演已经非常稀有，再加上迪士尼在城堡上配上动画、音效、喷泉及烟花的效果，真的精彩绝伦。如果是冬天观看，城堡上喷出的火让人有一种暖暖的爆炸感。
《冰雪奇缘》看了这个演出才去看电影，演出非常棒。带小朋友的更加不能错过，还有互动哦~2020年去的时候，演出也改良了，还加了雪花的场景，整个剧场飘满雪花，可想而知，小朋友们疯狂了。
《风暴来临》打斗很精彩，但是不血腥。杰克船长从高空坠下、被海上风暴卷起来都非常精彩，为他捏一把冷汗。
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 
《人猿泰山》演出加杂技，讲述了泰山从小到大的经历，难度挺高，演出人员非常敬业。官网上没有找到相关的介绍，可能是暂停了。
买票通道
刚开始都在携C上买，后来发现其实价格并不便宜。
如果是淡季去，建议直接购买正常门票即可，不用买快速通道。
如果是旺季去，懒人的话建议买套票，包含了8个热门项目的快速通道门票，绝对值得。
旺季去，自己也不想买快速通道的话，可以在官方APP上领取电子快速通行证，2次领取需间隔2小时，又或者前一张快速通行证使用完成才能再领取，先到先得，发完为止。如果发完还有项目想走快速通道，可以买单独的快速通行证。

…………………2021年12月游玩流程………………
1、由于疫情总是反反复复，预订好门票后，还是需要预约码，在订完票后会给你一个预约的链接，进入后：
（1）绑定你购买门票的订单编号
（2）选择到访日期，就是你要去玩的日期
（3）填写游客信息，包括：姓名、游客类型、证件号码和手机号码
这里可以绑定多张门票，我们每次过去都是我一个人来操作，第一次操作可以有点繁琐，按照步骤一步一步来，别急！
2、入园前准备好：身份证+健康码+预约码，一般流程是：第一道门先看健康码，第二道门看预约码，最后刷身份证，然后给你拍照绑定门票，这个时候纸质的门票就会给你，可以入场啦～
3、拿到纸质门票后，打开“迪士尼度假区”APP，把门票绑定到APP里面，这样你可以预约游玩项目，还有参加他们的活动，有的项目人多时，必须要在app上预约才能玩，否则要到15:30才行，都不让你排队，所以去之前，app要下载好哦～我们当天参加app活动，还抽到了创•极速光轮的快速通道，大家别错过！
4、如果你去的时候是你的生日月（比如你12月9日生日，那你在12月任何一天去迪士尼，都是你的生日月），可以拿着你的身份证到进门后的服务中心拿生日贴纸和徽章，在玩的时候工作人员会祝你生日快乐，还有可能会赠送一些意外的惊喜哦～
5、今年是迪士尼5周年，所以节目都有生日的氛围，比如花车巡游时会有一个大蛋糕花车，园内也都是生日氛围，很happy～
6、我们是周日去的，可能是早鸟票比较便宜，人不算特别少，有的热门项目排队30分钟还是有的，不过，这个旺季比起来，还是很空的，所以12月是个可以畅游的时间，我有朋友这点时间去玩，则表示人不多。
去的次数多也就熟门熟路的感觉，大家有问题的可以评论区问我哦～
